# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```

# rust-ini 0.21.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/latest

# INI in Rust

[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".

This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).

```
[]
 = "0.21"
```
## Usage

- Create a Ini configuration file.

```
extern crate ini;
use Ini;
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`

```
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green
unicode=Raspberry\x6811\x8393
[Book]
name=Rust cool
```
- Read from file `conf.ini`

```
use Ini;
```
- More details could be found in `examples`.

# cfg_if - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cfg-if/^1.0/

## Expand description

A macro for defining `#[cfg]` if-else statements.

The macro provided by this crate, `cfg_if`, is similar to the `if/elif` C
preprocessor macro by allowing definition of a cascade of `#[cfg]` cases,
emitting the implementation which matches first.

This allows you to conveniently provide a long list `#[cfg]`’d blocks of code
without having to rewrite each clause multiple times.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
cfg_if::cfg_if! {
    if #[cfg(unix)] {
        fn foo() { /* unix specific functionality */ }
    } else if #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")] {
        fn foo() { /* non-unix, 32-bit functionality */ }
    } else {
        fn foo() { /* fallback implementation */ }
    }
}
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [cfg_if](https://docs.rs/macro.cfg_if.html)
- The main macro provided by this crate. See crate documentation for more information.

# unicase - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicase/^2.6/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#unicase)UniCase

UniCase provides a way of specifying strings that are case-insensitive.

UniCase supports full [Unicode case
folding](https://www.w3.org/International/wiki/Case_folding). It can also
utilize faster ASCII case comparisons, if both strings are ASCII.

Using the `UniCase::new()` constructor will check the string to see if it
is all ASCII. When a `UniCase` is compared against another, if both are
ASCII, it will use the faster comparison.

There also exists the `Ascii` type in this crate, which will always assume
to use the ASCII case comparisons, if the encoding is already known.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use unicase::UniCase;
let a = UniCase::new("Maße");
let b = UniCase::new("MASSE");
let c = UniCase::new("mase");
assert_eq!(a, b);
assert!(b != c);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#ascii)Ascii

```
use unicase::Ascii;
let a = Ascii::new("foobar");
let b = Ascii::new("FoObAr");
assert_eq!(a, b);
```

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (4c9d2bfe4 2026-07-01)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# hanzo_ml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hanzo-ml/0.11.41/hanzo_ml/

## Expand description

ML framework for Rust

```
use hanzo_ml::{Tensor, DType, Device};
let a = Tensor::arange(0f32, 6f32, &Device::Cpu)?.reshape((2, 3))?;
let b = Tensor::arange(0f32, 12f32, &Device::Cpu)?.reshape((3, 4))?;
let c = a.matmul(&b)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- Simple syntax (looks and feels like PyTorch)
- CPU and Cuda backends (and M1 support)
- Enable serverless (CPU) small and fast deployments
- Model training
- Distributed computing (NCCL).
- Models out of the box (Llama, Whisper, Falcon, …)

[§](https://docs.rs#faq)FAQ

- Why Hanzo?

Hanzo stems from the need to reduce binary size in order to *enable serverless*
possible by making the whole engine smaller than PyTorch very large library volume

And simply *removing Python* from production workloads.
Python can really add overhead in more complex workflows and the [GIL](https://www.backblaze.com/blog/the-python-gil-past-present-and-future/) is a notorious source of headaches.

Rust is cool, and a lot of the HF ecosystem already has Rust crates [safetensors](https://github.com/huggingface/safetensors) and [tokenizers](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers)

[§](https://docs.rs#other-crates)Other Crates

Hanzo consists of a number of crates. This crate holds core the common data structures but you may wish to look at the docs for the other crates which can be found here:

- [hanzo-ml](https://docs.rs/hanzo-ml/). Core Datastructures and DataTypes.
- [hanzo-nn](https://docs.rs/hanzo-nn/). Building blocks for Neural Nets.
- [hanzo-datasets](https://docs.rs/hanzo-datasets/). Rust access to commonly used Datasets like MNIST.
- [hanzo-ml-examples](https://docs.rs/hanzo-ml-examples/). Examples of Hanzo in Use.
- [hanzo-onnx](https://docs.rs/hanzo-onnx/). Loading and using ONNX models.
- [hanzo-ml-pyo3](https://docs.rs/hanzo-ml-pyo3/). Access to Hanzo from Python.
- [hanzo-transformers](https://docs.rs/hanzo-transformers/). Hanzo implementation of many published transformer models.

- Tensor Layouts including contiguous or sparse strides

- Model merging and delta-compression utilities, implemented natively on top of
the `hanzo-ml`tensor + safetensors APIs (no Python, no external tooling).

- Numpy support for tensors.

- Tensor Operation Enums and Traits

- Just enough pickle support to be able to read PyTorch checkpoints.
- [quantized](https://docs.rs/quantized/index.html)

- Module to load `safetensor`files into CPU/GPU memory.

- TensorScalar Enum and Trait

- The shape of a tensor is a tuple with the size of each of its dimensions.

- StreamTensror useful for streaming ops.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/test_utils/index.html)- utils
- [utils](https://docs.rs/utils/index.html)
- Useful functions for checking features.

# snowbridge_pallet_system_frontend - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/snowbridge-pallet-system-frontend/0.11.0/snowbridge_pallet_system_frontend/

## Expand description

System frontend pallet that acts as the user-facing control-plane for Snowbridge.

Some operations are delegated to a backend pallet installed on a remote parachain.

[§](https://docs.rs#extrinsics)Extrinsics

- `Call::register_token`

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# sortcrab - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sortcrab/0.1.3/sortcrab/

## Expand description

sortcrab — file organization library.

sortcrab scans a source directory, classifies each file by its extension,
computes an academic semester from the file’s modification time, and moves
it into a structured destination tree:
`{target}/{category}/{subcategory}/{semester}/{filename}`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use sortcrab::core::sort_files;
use sortcrab::config::rules::RulesConfig;
use sortcrab::config::SemesterConfig;
use std::path::Path;
let rules = RulesConfig::default();
let semester = SemesterConfig::default();
let report = sort_files(
    Path::new("/path/to/source"),
    Path::new("/path/to/target"),
    &rules,
    false,
    &semester,
)?;
println!("Moved {} files", report.moved);
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [cli](https://docs.rs/cli/index.html)
- CLI argument parsing and command dispatch.
- [config](https://docs.rs/config/index.html)
- Configuration loading, saving, and path resolution.
- [core](https://docs.rs/core/index.html)
- Core domain logic: classification, file moving, semester computation, and orchestration.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types for sortcrab operations.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [init_](https://docs.rs/fn.init_logging.html)- logging
- Initialize logging based on verbosity level.
- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Run the sortcrab CLI.

# winit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fission-winit/0.30.13-fission.1/winit/

## Expand description

Winit is a cross-platform window creation and event loop management library.

[§](https://docs.rs#building-windows)Building windows

Before you can create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html), you first need to build an

[. This is done with the](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[function.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.new)

`EventLoop::new()````
use winit::event_loop::EventLoop;
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ...
}
```
Then you create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) with

[.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.create_window)

`create_window`[§](https://docs.rs#event-handling)Event handling

Once a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) has been created, it will generate different

*events*. A

[object can generate](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[s when certain input events occur, such as a cursor moving over the window or a key getting pressed while the window is focused. Devices can generate](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html)

`WindowEvent`[s, which contain unfiltered event data that isn’t specific to a certain window. Some user activity, like mouse movement, can generate both a](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`

`WindowEvent`*and*a

[. You can also create and handle your own custom](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`[s, if desired.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.UserEvent)

`Event::UserEvent`You can retrieve events by calling [ EventLoop::run_app()](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.run_app). This function will
dispatch events for every

[that was created with that particular](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[, and will run until](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[is used, at which point](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.exit)

`exit()`[.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.LoopExiting)

`Event::LoopExiting`Winit no longer uses a `EventLoop::poll_events() -> impl Iterator<Event>`-based event loop
model, since that can’t be implemented properly on some platforms (e.g web, iOS) and works
poorly on most other platforms. However, this model can be re-implemented to an extent with
`EventLoopExtPumpEvents::pump_app_events()` 1. See that method’s documentation for more reasons about why
it’s discouraged beyond compatibility reasons.

```
use winit::application::ApplicationHandler;
use winit::event::WindowEvent;
use winit::event_loop::{ActiveEventLoop, ControlFlow, EventLoop};
use winit::window::{Window, WindowId};
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
    window: Option<Window>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
    fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
        self.window = Some(event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap());
    }
    fn window_event(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {
        match event {
            WindowEvent::CloseRequested => {
                println!("The close button was pressed; stopping");
                event_loop.exit();
            },
            WindowEvent::RedrawRequested => {
                // Redraw the application.
                //
                // It's preferable for applications that do not render continuously to render in
                // this event rather than in AboutToWait, since rendering in here allows
                // the program to gracefully handle redraws requested by the OS.
                // Draw.
                // Queue a RedrawRequested event.
                //
                // You only need to call this if you've determined that you need to redraw in
                // applications which do not always need to. Applications that redraw continuously
                // can render here instead.
                self.window.as_ref().unwrap().request_redraw();
            }
            _ => (),
        }
    }
}
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ControlFlow::Poll continuously runs the event loop, even if the OS hasn't
    // dispatched any events. This is ideal for games and similar applications.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Poll);
    // ControlFlow::Wait pauses the event loop if no events are available to process.
    // This is ideal for non-game applications that only update in response to user
    // input, and uses significantly less power/CPU time than ControlFlow::Poll.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Wait);
    let mut app = App::default();
    event_loop.run_app(&mut app);
}
```
[ WindowEvent](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html) has a

[member. In multi-window environments, it should be compared to the value returned by](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowId.html)

`WindowId`[to determine which](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.id)

`Window::id()`[dispatched the event.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[§](https://docs.rs#drawing-on-the-window)Drawing on the window

Winit doesn’t directly provide any methods for drawing on a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html). However, it allows you
to retrieve the raw handle of the window and display (see the

[module and/or the](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html)

`platform`[and](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_window_handle)

`raw_window_handle`[methods), which in turn allows you to create an OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX/Metal/etc. context that can be used to render graphics.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_display_handle)

`raw_display_handle`Note that many platforms will display garbage data in the window’s client area if the
application doesn’t render anything to the window by the time the desktop compositor is ready to
display the window to the user. If you notice this happening, you should create the window with
[ visible set to false](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowAttributes.html#method.with_visible) and explicitly make
the window visible only once you’re ready to render into it.

[§](https://docs.rs#ui-scaling)UI scaling

UI scaling is important, go read the docs for the [ dpi](https://docs.rs/dpi/index.html) crate for an
introduction.

All of Winit’s functions return physical types, but can take either logical or physical coordinates as input, allowing you to use the most convenient coordinate system for your particular application.

Winit will dispatch a [ ScaleFactorChanged](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged) event whenever a window’s scale factor has changed.
This can happen if the user drags their window from a standard-resolution monitor to a high-DPI
monitor or if the user changes their DPI settings. This allows you to rescale your application’s
UI elements and adjust how the platform changes the window’s size to reflect the new scale
factor. If a window hasn’t received a

[event, its scale factor can be found by calling](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged)

`ScaleFactorChanged`[.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.scale_factor)

`window.scale_factor()`[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo Features

Winit provides the following Cargo features:

- `x11`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the X11 backend.
- `wayland`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the Wayland backend.
- `rwh_04`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.4`traits.
- `rwh_05`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.5`traits.
- `rwh_06`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.6`traits.
- `serde`: Enables serialization/deserialization of certain types with- [Serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde).
- `mint`: Enables mint (math interoperability standard types) conversions.

See the [ platform](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html) module for documentation on platform-specific cargo
features.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [rwh_05](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/i686-pc-windows-msvc/raw_window_handle/index.html)as raw_window_handle_05;- `rwh_05`

# hanzo-kernel 0.2.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/hanzo-kernel/0.2.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/hanzo-kernel/0.2.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

hanzo-kernel: Hanzo's first-party GPU kernel DSL.

Write a kernel ONCE in Rust; it lowers to CUDA / ROCm / Vulkan / Metal. This crate is the
first-party facade over the CubeCL lowering engine: kernel source names only `hanzo_kernel::*`,
never `cubecl`. "Values, not places" -- CubeCL is the implementation value; `hanzo_kernel` is the
stable namespace we build against, so the engine can be upgraded (or forked) without touching a
single kernel.

The perf primitives our hand-tuned kernels rely on are all here and lower to the native instruction on each backend:

- `dot`on a vectorized- `Line<i8>`-> dp4a / OpSDotAccSat (int8 4-way dot)
- `cmma`-> tensor cores (WMMA / cooperative-matrix / simdgroup)
- `SharedMemory`,- `plane_*`(subgroup reduce/shuffle),- `Atomic`, barriers

MIGRATION POLICY (perf-gated, never a downgrade): the DSL provides COVERAGE -- every quant type on every backend, from one source, killing the "same op, N impls, N numeric behaviors" bug class. A hand-tuned kernel is replaced by its DSL twin ONLY when the DSL version is bit-exact AND within perf noise (bench-gated). Where a hand-tuned kernel still wins, it stays as the specialized peak path and the DSL is the portable fallback for the backends that lack a tuned version.

---

# rust-ini 0.21.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.21.3

# INI in Rust

[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".

This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).

```
[]
 = "0.21"
```
## Usage

- Create a Ini configuration file.

```
extern crate ini;
use Ini;
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`

```
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green
unicode=Raspberry\x6811\x8393
[Book]
name=Rust cool
```
- Read from file `conf.ini`

```
use Ini;
```
- More details could be found in `examples`.

# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.21.3/target-redirect/ini/

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ini](https://docs.rs/struct.Ini.html)
- Ini struct
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)- Error
- Parse error
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseOption.html)- Option
- Parsing configuration
- [Properties](https://docs.rs/struct.Properties.html)
- Properties type (key-value pairs)
- [Properties](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertiesIntoIter.html)- Into - Iter
- [Property](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyIter.html)- Iter
- [Property](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyIterMut.html)- Iter - Mut

                    from currently. You should check the

### default

This feature flag does not enable additional features.

### inline-comment

# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/0.21.3/ini/index.html

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```

[65](#65)#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Copy, Clone)]
[67](#67)pub enum EscapePolicy {
[68](#68)    Nothing,
[70](#70)    Basics,
[74](#74)    BasicsUnicode,
[78](#78)    BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[81](#81)    Reserved,
[84](#84)    ReservedUnicode,
[87](#87)    ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[89](#89)    Everything,
[91](#91)}
[92](#92)
[93](#93)impl EscapePolicy {
[94](#94)    fn escape_basics(self) -> bool {
[95](#95)        self != EscapePolicy::Nothing
[96](#96)    }
[97](#97)
[98](#98)    fn escape_reserved(self) -> bool {
[99](#99)        matches!(
[100](#100)            self,
[101](#101)            EscapePolicy::Reserved
[102](#102)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode
[103](#103)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended
[104](#104)                | EscapePolicy::Everything
[105](#105)        )
[106](#106)    }
[107](#107)
[108](#108)    fn escape_unicode(self) -> bool {
[109](#109)        matches!(
[110](#110)            self,
[111](#111)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode
[112](#112)                | EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended
[113](#113)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode
[114](#114)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended
[115](#115)                | EscapePolicy::Everything
[116](#116)        )
[117](#117)    }
[118](#118)
[119](#119)    fn escape_unicode_extended(self) -> bool {
[120](#120)        matches!(
[121](#121)            self,
[122](#122)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended | EscapePolicy::Everything
[123](#123)        )
[124](#124)    }
[125](#125)
[126](#126)    pub fn should_escape(self, c: char) -> bool {
[129](#129)        match c {
[130](#130)            '\\' | '\x00'..='\x1f' | '\x7f' => self.escape_basics(),
[133](#133)            ';' | '#' | '=' | ':' => self.escape_reserved(),
[134](#134)            '\u{0080}'..='\u{FFFF}' => self.escape_unicode(),
[135](#135)            '\u{10000}'..='\u{10FFFF}' => self.escape_unicode_extended(),
[136](#136)            _ => false,
[137](#137)        }
[138](#138)    }
[139](#139)}
[140](#140)
[141](#141)fn escape_str(s: &str, policy: EscapePolicy) -> String {
[158](#158)    let mut escaped: String = String::with_capacity(s.len());
[159](#159)    for c in s.chars() {
[160](#160)        if !policy.should_escape(c) {
[163](#163)            escaped.push(c);
[164](#164)            continue;
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)
[167](#167)        match c {
[168](#168)            '\\' => escaped.push_str("\\\\"),
[169](#169)            '\0' => escaped.push_str("\\0"),
[170](#170)            '\x01'..='\x06' | '\x0e'..='\x1f' | '\x7f'..='\u{00ff}' => {
[171](#171)                escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:04x}", c as isize)[..])
[172](#172)            }
[173](#173)            '\x07' => escaped.push_str("\\a"),
[174](#174)            '\x08' => escaped.push_str("\\b"),
[175](#175)            '\x0c' => escaped.push_str("\\f"),
[176](#176)            '\x0b' => escaped.push_str("\\v"),
[177](#177)            '\n' => escaped.push_str("\\n"),
[178](#178)            '\t' => escaped.push_str("\\t"),
[179](#179)            '\r' => escaped.push_str("\\r"),
[180](#180)            '\u{0080}'..='\u{FFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:04x}", c as isize)[..]),
[181](#181)            '\u{10000}'..='\u{FFFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:05x}", c as isize)[..]),
[183](#183)            '\u{100000}'..='\u{10FFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:06x}", c as isize)[..]),
[184](#184)            _ => {
[185](#185)                escaped.push('\\');
[186](#186)                escaped.push(c);
[187](#187)            }
[188](#188)        }
[189](#189)    }
[190](#190)    escaped
[191](#191)}

[325](#325)        }

[331](#331)        }
[332](#332)
[333](#333)        macro_rules! section_key {
[334](#334)            ($s:expr) => {
[335](#335)                $s.map(|s| UniCase::from(s.into()))
[336](#336)            };
[337](#337)        }

[339](#339)    } else {
[340](#340)        pub type SectionKey = Option<String>;

[346](#346)            ($s:expr) => {
[347](#347)                $s

[355](#355)        }

[376](#376)    pub fn set<'b, K, V>(&'b mut self, key: K, value: V) -> &'b mut SectionSetter<'a>

[379](#379)        K: Into<String>,
[380](#380)        V: Into<String>,
[381](#381)        'a: 'b,

[389](#389)    }

[404](#404)    }

[406](#406)    pub fn delete<'b, K>(&'b mut self, key: &K) -> &'b mut SectionSetter<'a>

[410](#410)        'a: 'b,

[417](#417)    }

[422](#422)            .section(self.section_name.as_ref())

[425](#425)    }

[932](#932)    pub fn write_to_file_opt<P: AsRef<Path>>(&self, filename: P, opt: WriteOption) -> io::Result<()> {
[934](#934)        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
[935](#935)            .write(true)
[936](#936)            .truncate(true)
[937](#937)            .create(true)
[938](#938)            .open(filename.as_ref())?;

[940](#940)    }
[941](#941)
[942](#942)    pub fn write_to<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W) -> io::Result<()> {
[944](#944)        self.write_to_opt(writer, Default::default())
[945](#945)    }
[946](#946)
[947](#947)    pub fn write_to_policy<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W, policy: EscapePolicy) -> io::Result<()> {
[949](#949)        self.write_to_opt(
[950](#950)            writer,
[951](#951)            WriteOption {
[952](#952)                escape_policy: policy,
[953](#953)                ..Default::default()
[954](#954)            },
[955](#955)        )
[956](#956)    }
[957](#957)
[958](#958)    pub fn write_to_opt<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W, opt: WriteOption) -> io::Result<()> {
[960](#960)        let mut firstline = true;
[961](#961)
[962](#962)        for (section, props) in &self.sections {
[963](#963)            if !props.data.is_empty() {
[964](#964)                if firstline {
[965](#965)                    firstline = false;
[966](#966)                } else {
[967](#967)                    writer.write_all(opt.line_separator.as_str().as_bytes())?;
[969](#969)                }
[970](#970)            }
[971](#971)
[972](#972)            if let Some(ref section) = *section {
[973](#973)                write!(
[974](#974)                    writer,
[975](#975)                    "[{}]{}",
[976](#976)                    escape_str(§ion[..], opt.escape_policy),
[977](#977)                    opt.line_separator
[978](#978)                )?;
[979](#979)            }
[980](#980)            for (k, v) in props.iter() {
[981](#981)                let k_str = escape_str(k, opt.escape_policy);
[982](#982)                let v_str = escape_str(v, opt.escape_policy);
[983](#983)                write!(writer, "{}{}{}{}", k_str, opt.kv_separator, v_str, opt.line_separator)?;
[984](#984)            }
[985](#985)        }
[986](#986)        Ok(())
[987](#987)    }
[988](#988)}

[1056](#1056)    pub fn load_from_file_opt<P: AsRef<Path>>(filename: P, opt: ParseOption) -> Result<Ini, Error> {
[1058](#1058)        let mut reader = match File::open(filename.as_ref()) {
[1059](#1059)            Err(e) => {
[1060](#1060)                return Err(Error::Io(e));
[1061](#1061)            }
[1062](#1062)            Ok(r) => r,
[1063](#1063)        };
[1064](#1064)
[1065](#1065)        let mut with_bom = false;
[1066](#1066)
[1067](#1067)        let mut bom = [0u8; 3];
[1070](#1070)        if reader.read_exact(&mut bom).is_ok() && &bom == b"\xEF\xBB\xBF" {
[1071](#1071)            with_bom = true;
[1072](#1072)        }
[1073](#1073)
[1074](#1074)        if !with_bom {
[1075](#1075)            reader.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;
[1077](#1077)        }
[1078](#1078)
[1079](#1079)        Ini::read_from_opt(&mut reader, opt)
[1080](#1080)    }

[1259](#1259)impl<'a> Parser<'a> {
[1260](#1260)    pub fn new(rdr: Chars<'a>, opt: ParseOption) -> Parser<'a> {
[1262](#1262)        let mut p = Parser {
[1263](#1263)            ch: None,
[1264](#1264)            line: 0,
[1265](#1265)            col: 0,
[1266](#1266)            rdr,
[1267](#1267)            opt,
[1268](#1268)        };
[1269](#1269)        p.bump();
[1270](#1270)        p
[1271](#1271)    }
[1272](#1272)
[1273](#1273)    fn bump(&mut self) {
[1274](#1274)        self.ch = self.rdr.next();
[1275](#1275)        match self.ch {
[1276](#1276)            Some('\n') => {
[1277](#1277)                self.line += 1;
[1278](#1278)                self.col = 0;
[1279](#1279)            }
[1280](#1280)            Some(..) => {
[1281](#1281)                self.col += 1;
[1282](#1282)            }
[1283](#1283)            None => {}
[1284](#1284)        }
[1285](#1285)    }
[1286](#1286)
[1287](#1287)    #[cold]
[1288](#1288)    #[inline(never)]
[1289](#1289)    fn error<U, M: Into<Cow<'static, str>>>(&self, msg: M) -> Result<U, ParseError> {
[1290](#1290)        Err(ParseError {
[1291](#1291)            line: self.line + 1,
[1292](#1292)            col: self.col + 1,
[1293](#1293)            msg: msg.into(),
[1294](#1294)        })
[1295](#1295)    }
[1296](#1296)
[1297](#1297)    #[cold]
[1298](#1298)    fn eof_error(&self, expecting: &[Option<char>]) -> Result<char, ParseError> {
[1299](#1299)        self.error(format!("expecting \"{:?}\" but found EOF.", expecting))
[1300](#1300)    }
[1301](#1301)
[1302](#1302)    fn char_or_eof(&self, expecting: &[Option<char>]) -> Result<char, ParseError> {
[1303](#1303)        match self.ch {
[1304](#1304)            Some(ch) => Ok(ch),
[1305](#1305)            None => self.eof_error(expecting),
[1306](#1306)        }
[1307](#1307)    }
[1308](#1308)
[1309](#1309)    fn parse_whitespace_preserve_line_leading(&mut self) {
[1329](#1329)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1330](#1330)            match c {
[1331](#1331)                ' ' | '\t' => {
[1333](#1333)                    self.bump();
[1334](#1334)                    }
[1338](#1338)                '\n' | '\r' => {
[1339](#1339)                    self.bump();
[1341](#1341)                    if matches!(self.ch, Some(' ') | Some('\t')) {
[1343](#1343)                        break;
[1345](#1345)                    }
[1346](#1346)                    }
[1348](#1348)                c if c.is_whitespace() => {
[1349](#1349)                    self.bump();
[1351](#1351)                }
[1352](#1352)                _ => break,
[1353](#1353)            }
[1354](#1354)        }
[1355](#1355)    }
[1356](#1356)
[1357](#1357)    fn parse_whitespace_except_line_break(&mut self) {
[1363](#1363)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1364](#1364)            if (c == '\n' || c == '\r' || !c.is_whitespace()) && c != '\t' {
[1365](#1365)                break;
[1366](#1366)            }
[1367](#1367)            self.bump();
[1368](#1368)        }
[1369](#1369)    }
[1370](#1370)
[1371](#1371)    pub fn parse(&mut self) -> Result<Ini, ParseError> {
[1373](#1373)        let mut result = Ini::new();
[1374](#1374)        let mut curkey: String = "".into();
[1375](#1375)        let mut cursec: Option<String> = None;
[1376](#1376)
[1377](#1377)        while let Some(cur_ch) = self.ch {
[1378](#1378)            match cur_ch {
[1379](#1379)                ';' | '#' => {
[1380](#1380)                    if cfg!(not(feature = "inline-comment")) {
[1381](#1381)                        if self.col > 1 {
[1385](#1385)                            return self.error("doesn't support inline comment");
[1386](#1386)                        }
[1387](#1387)                    }
[1388](#1388)
[1389](#1389)                    self.parse_comment();
[1390](#1390)                }
[1391](#1391)                '[' => match self.parse_section() {
[1392](#1392)                    Ok(mut sec) => {
[1393](#1393)                        trim_in_place(&mut sec);
[1394](#1394)                        cursec = Some(sec);
[1395](#1395)                        match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1396](#1396)                            SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1397](#1397)                                v.insert(Default::default());
[1398](#1398)                            }
[1399](#1399)                            SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1400](#1400)                                o.append(Default::default());
[1401](#1401)                            }
[1402](#1402)                        }
[1403](#1403)                    }
[1404](#1404)                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1405](#1405)                },
[1406](#1406)                '=' | ':' => {
[1407](#1407)                    if (curkey[..]).is_empty() {
[1408](#1408)                        return self.error("missing key");
[1409](#1409)                    }
[1410](#1410)                    match self.parse_val() {
[1411](#1411)                        Ok(mval) => {
[1412](#1412)                            match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1413](#1413)                                SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1414](#1414)                                    let mut prop = Properties::new();
[1416](#1416)                                    prop.insert(curkey, mval);
[1417](#1417)                                    v.insert(prop);
[1418](#1418)                                }
[1419](#1419)                                SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1420](#1420)                                    o.last_mut().append(curkey, mval);
[1422](#1422)                                }
[1423](#1423)                            }
[1424](#1424)                            curkey = "".into();
[1425](#1425)                        }
[1426](#1426)                        Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1427](#1427)                    }
[1428](#1428)                }
[1429](#1429)                ' ' | '\t' => {
[1430](#1430)                    let mut consumed_whitespace = String::new();
[1432](#1432)                    while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1433](#1433)                        if c == ' ' || c == '\t' {
[1434](#1434)                            consumed_whitespace.push(c);
[1435](#1435)                            self.bump();
[1436](#1436)                        } else {
[1437](#1437)                            break;
[1438](#1438)                        }
[1439](#1439)                    }
[1440](#1440)
[1441](#1441)                    match self.ch {
[1443](#1443)                        Some('[') => {
[1444](#1444)                            match self.parse_section() {
[1446](#1446)                                Ok(mut sec) => {
[1447](#1447)                                    trim_in_place(&mut sec);
[1448](#1448)                                    cursec = Some(sec);
[1449](#1449)                                    match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1450](#1450)                                        SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1451](#1451)                                            v.insert(Default::default());
[1452](#1452)                                        }
[1453](#1453)                                        SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1454](#1454)                                            o.append(Default::default());
[1455](#1455)                                        }
[1456](#1456)                                    }
[1457](#1457)                                }
[1458](#1458)                                Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1459](#1459)                            }
[1460](#1460)                        }
[1461](#1461)                        Some('\n') | Some('\r') => {
[1462](#1462)                            self.bump(); continue;
[1465](#1465)                        }
[1466](#1466)                        _ => {
[1467](#1467)                            match self.parse_str_until(&[Some('='), Some(':')], false) {
[1469](#1469)                                Ok(key_part) => {
[1470](#1470)                                    let mut mkey = if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1471](#1471)                                        consumed_whitespace + &key_part
[1472](#1472)                                    } else {
[1473](#1473)                                        key_part
[1474](#1474)                                    };
[1475](#1475)
[1476](#1476)                                    if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1478](#1478)                                        trim_end_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1479](#1479)                                    } else {
[1480](#1480)                                        trim_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1481](#1481)                                    }
[1482](#1482)                                    curkey = mkey;
[1483](#1483)                                }
[1484](#1484)                                Err(_) => {
[1485](#1485)                                    }
[1488](#1488)                            }
[1489](#1489)                        }
[1490](#1490)                    }
[1491](#1491)                }
[1492](#1492)                '\n' | '\r' => {
[1493](#1493)                    self.bump();
[1495](#1495)                }
[1496](#1496)                _ => match self.parse_key() {
[1497](#1497)                    Ok(mut mkey) => {
[1498](#1498)                        if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1501](#1501)                            trim_end_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1502](#1502)                        } else {
[1503](#1503)                            trim_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1504](#1504)                        }
[1505](#1505)                        curkey = mkey;
[1506](#1506)                    }
[1507](#1507)                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1508](#1508)                },
[1509](#1509)            }
[1510](#1510)
[1511](#1511)            self.parse_whitespace_preserve_line_leading();
[1514](#1514)        }
[1515](#1515)
[1516](#1516)        Ok(result)
[1517](#1517)    }
[1518](#1518)
[1519](#1519)    fn parse_comment(&mut self) {
[1520](#1520)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1521](#1521)            self.bump();
[1522](#1522)            if c == '\n' {
[1523](#1523)                break;
[1524](#1524)            }
[1525](#1525)        }
[1526](#1526)    }
[1527](#1527)
[1528](#1528)    fn parse_str_until(&mut self, endpoint: &[Option<char>], check_inline_comment: bool) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1529](#1529)        let mut result: String = String::new();
[1530](#1530)
[1531](#1531)        let mut in_line_continuation = false;
[1532](#1532)
[1533](#1533)        while !endpoint.contains(&self.ch) {
[1534](#1534)            match self.char_or_eof(endpoint)? {
[1535](#1535)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1536](#1536)                ch if check_inline_comment && (ch == ' ' || ch == '\t') => {
[1537](#1537)                    self.bump();
[1538](#1538)
[1539](#1539)                    match self.ch {
[1540](#1540)                        Some('#') | Some(';') => {
[1541](#1541)                            self.parse_comment();
[1543](#1543)                            if in_line_continuation {
[1544](#1544)                                result.push(ch);
[1545](#1545)                                continue;
[1546](#1546)                            } else {
[1547](#1547)                                break;
[1548](#1548)                            }
[1549](#1549)                        }
[1550](#1550)                        Some(_) => {
[1551](#1551)                            result.push(ch);
[1552](#1552)                            continue;
[1553](#1553)                        }
[1554](#1554)                        None => {
[1555](#1555)                            result.push(ch);
[1556](#1556)                        }
[1557](#1557)                    }
[1558](#1558)                }
[1559](#1559)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1560](#1560)                ch if check_inline_comment && in_line_continuation && (ch == '#' || ch == ';') => {
[1561](#1561)                    self.parse_comment();
[1562](#1562)                    continue;
[1563](#1563)                }
[1564](#1564)                '\\' => {
[1565](#1565)                    self.bump();
[1566](#1566)                    let Some(ch) = self.ch else {
[1567](#1567)                        result.push('\\');
[1568](#1568)                        continue;
[1569](#1569)                    };
[1570](#1570)
[1571](#1571)                    if matches!(ch, '\n') {
[1572](#1572)                        in_line_continuation = true;
[1573](#1573)                    } else if self.opt.enabled_escape {
[1574](#1574)                        match ch {
[1575](#1575)                            '0' => result.push('\0'),
[1576](#1576)                            'a' => result.push('\x07'),
[1577](#1577)                            'b' => result.push('\x08'),
[1578](#1578)                            't' => result.push('\t'),
[1579](#1579)                            'r' => result.push('\r'),
[1580](#1580)                            'n' => result.push('\n'),
[1581](#1581)                            '\n' => self.bump(),
[1582](#1582)                            'x' => {
[1583](#1583)                                let mut code: String = String::with_capacity(4);
[1585](#1585)                                for _ in 0..4 {
[1586](#1586)                                    self.bump();
[1587](#1587)                                    let ch = self.char_or_eof(endpoint)?;
[1588](#1588)                                    if ch == '\\' {
[1589](#1589)                                        self.bump();
[1590](#1590)                                        if self.ch != Some('\n') {
[1591](#1591)                                            return self.error(format!(
[1592](#1592)                                                "expecting \"\\\\n\" but \
[1593](#1593)                                             found \"{:?}\".",
[1594](#1594)                                                self.ch
[1595](#1595)                                            ));
[1596](#1596)                                        }
[1597](#1597)                                    }
[1598](#1598)
[1599](#1599)                                    code.push(ch);
[1600](#1600)                                }
[1601](#1601)                                let r = u32::from_str_radix(&code[..], 16);
[1602](#1602)                                match r.ok().and_then(char::from_u32) {
[1603](#1603)                                    Some(ch) => result.push(ch),
[1604](#1604)                                    None => return self.error("unknown character in \\xHH form"),
[1605](#1605)                                }
[1606](#1606)                            }
[1607](#1607)                            c => result.push(c),
[1608](#1608)                        }
[1609](#1609)                    } else {
[1610](#1610)                        result.push('\\');
[1611](#1611)                        result.push(ch);
[1612](#1612)                    }
[1613](#1613)                }
[1614](#1614)                ch => result.push(ch),
[1615](#1615)            }
[1616](#1616)            self.bump();
[1617](#1617)        }
[1618](#1618)
[1619](#1619)        let _ = check_inline_comment;
[1620](#1620)        let _ = in_line_continuation;
[1621](#1621)
[1622](#1622)        Ok(result)
[1623](#1623)    }
[1624](#1624)
[1625](#1625)    fn parse_section(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1626](#1626)        cfg_if! {
[1627](#1627)            if #[cfg(feature = "brackets-in-section-names")] {
[1628](#1628)                self.bump();
[1630](#1630)
[1631](#1631)                let mut s = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\r'), Some('\n')], cfg!(feature = "inline-comment"))?;
[1632](#1632)
[1633](#1633)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1635](#1635)                if matches!(self.ch, Some('#') | Some(';')) {
[1636](#1636)                    self.parse_comment();
[1637](#1637)                }
[1638](#1638)
[1639](#1639)                let tr = s.trim_end_matches([' ', '\t']);
[1640](#1640)                if !tr.ends_with(']') {
[1641](#1641)                    return self.error("section must be ended with ']'");
[1642](#1642)                }
[1643](#1643)
[1644](#1644)                s.truncate(tr.len() - 1);
[1645](#1645)                Ok(s)
[1646](#1646)            } else {
[1647](#1647)                self.bump();
[1649](#1649)                let sec = self.parse_str_until(&[Some(']')], false)?;
[1650](#1650)                if let Some(']') = self.ch {
[1651](#1651)                    self.bump();
[1652](#1652)                }
[1653](#1653)
[1654](#1654)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1656](#1656)                if matches!(self.ch, Some('#') | Some(';')) {
[1657](#1657)                    self.parse_comment();
[1658](#1658)                }
[1659](#1659)
[1660](#1660)                Ok(sec)
[1661](#1661)            }
[1662](#1662)        }
[1663](#1663)    }
[1664](#1664)
[1665](#1665)    fn parse_key(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1670](#1670)        self.parse_str_until(&[Some('='), Some(':')], false)
[1671](#1671)    }
[1672](#1672)
[1673](#1673)    fn parse_val(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1674](#1674)        self.bump();
[1675](#1675)        self.parse_whitespace_except_line_break();
[1677](#1677)
[1678](#1678)        let mut val = String::new();
[1679](#1679)        let mut val_first_part = true;
[1680](#1680)        'parse_value_line_loop: loop {
[1682](#1682)            match self.ch {
[1683](#1683)                None => break,
[1685](#1685)
[1686](#1686)                Some('"') if self.opt.enabled_quote => {
[1688](#1688)                    self.bump();
[1690](#1690)                    let quoted_val = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('"')], false)?;
[1692](#1692)                    val.push_str("ed_val);
[1693](#1693)
[1694](#1694)                    self.bump();
[1696](#1696)
[1697](#1697)                    val_first_part = false;
[1699](#1699)                    continue;
[1700](#1700)                }
[1701](#1701)
[1702](#1702)                Some('\'') if self.opt.enabled_quote => {
[1704](#1704)                    self.bump();
[1706](#1706)                    let quoted_val = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\'')], false)?;
[1708](#1708)                    val.push_str("ed_val);
[1709](#1709)
[1710](#1710)                    self.bump();
[1712](#1712)
[1713](#1713)                    val_first_part = false;
[1715](#1715)                    continue;
[1716](#1716)                }
[1717](#1717)
[1718](#1718)                _ => {
[1720](#1720)                    let standard_val = self.parse_str_until_eol(cfg!(feature = "inline-comment"))?;
[1722](#1722)
[1723](#1723)                    let trimmed_value = if val_first_part {
[1724](#1724)                        standard_val.trim()
[1726](#1726)                    } else {
[1727](#1727)                        standard_val.trim_end()
[1729](#1729)                    };
[1730](#1730)                    val_first_part = false;
[1731](#1731)
[1732](#1732)                    val.push_str(trimmed_value);
[1733](#1733)
[1734](#1734)                    if self.opt.enabled_indented_mutiline_value {
[1735](#1735)                        self.bump();
[1737](#1737)
[1738](#1738)                        loop {
[1739](#1739)                            match self.ch {
[1740](#1740)                                Some(' ') | Some('\t') => {
[1741](#1741)                                    self.parse_whitespace_except_line_break();
[1744](#1744)                                    val.push('\n');
[1746](#1746)                                    continue 'parse_value_line_loop;
[1748](#1748)                                }
[1749](#1749)
[1750](#1750)                                Some('\r') => {
[1751](#1751)                                    self.bump();
[1753](#1753)                                    if self.ch == Some('\n') {
[1754](#1754)                                        self.bump();
[1755](#1755)                                        val.push('\n');
[1756](#1756)                                    } else {
[1757](#1757)                                        return self.error("\\r is not followed by \\n");
[1759](#1759)                                    }
[1760](#1760)                                }
[1761](#1761)
[1762](#1762)                                Some('\n') => {
[1763](#1763)                                    self.bump();
[1765](#1765)                                    val.push('\n');
[1766](#1766)                                }
[1767](#1767)
[1768](#1768)                                _ => break 'parse_value_line_loop,
[1770](#1770)                            }
[1771](#1771)                        }
[1772](#1772)                    } else {
[1773](#1773)                        break;
[1774](#1774)                    }
[1775](#1775)                }
[1776](#1776)            }
[1777](#1777)        }
[1778](#1778)
[1779](#1779)        if self.opt.enabled_indented_mutiline_value {
[1780](#1780)            trim_line_feeds(&mut val);
[1782](#1782)        }
[1783](#1783)
[1784](#1784)        Ok(val)
[1785](#1785)    }
[1786](#1786)
[1787](#1787)    #[inline]
[1788](#1788)    fn parse_str_until_eol(&mut self, check_inline_comment: bool) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1789](#1789)        self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\n'), Some('\r'), None], check_inline_comment)
[1790](#1790)    }
[1791](#1791)}
[1792](#1792)
[1793](#1793)fn trim_in_place(string: &mut String) {
[1794](#1794)    string.truncate(string.trim_end().len());
[1795](#1795)    string.drain(..(string.len() - string.trim_start().len()));
[1796](#1796)}
[1797](#1797)
[1798](#1798)fn trim_end_in_place(string: &mut String) {
[1799](#1799)    string.truncate(string.trim_end().len());
[1800](#1800)}
[1801](#1801)
[1802](#1802)fn trim_line_feeds(string: &mut String) {
[1803](#1803)    const LF: char = '\n';
[1804](#1804)    string.truncate(string.trim_end_matches(LF).len());
[1805](#1805)    string.drain(..(string.len() - string.trim_start_matches(LF).len()));
[1806](#1806)}

[2217](#2217)    fn load_from_str_with_crlf() {

[2219](#2219)        let opt = Ini::load_from_str(input);
[2220](#2220)        assert!(opt.is_ok());
[2221](#2221)
[2222](#2222)        let output = opt.unwrap();

[2224](#2224)        assert!(output.section(None::<String>).is_some());
[2225](#2225)        let sec1 = output.section(None::<String>).unwrap();

[2227](#2227)        let key1: String = "key1".into();
[2228](#2228)        assert!(sec1.contains_key(&key1));

[2234](#2234)        assert_eq!(sec1[&key2], val2);

[2496](#2496)    #[test]
[2497](#2497)    fn write_line_separator() {
[2498](#2498)        use std::str;
[2499](#2499)
[2500](#2500)        let mut ini = Ini::new();
[2501](#2501)        ini.with_section(Some("Section1"))
[2502](#2502)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2503](#2503)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2504](#2504)        ini.with_section(Some("Section2"))
[2505](#2505)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2506](#2506)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2507](#2507)
[2508](#2508)        {
[2509](#2509)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2510](#2510)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2511](#2511)                &mut buf,
[2512](#2512)                WriteOption {
[2513](#2513)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::CR,
[2514](#2514)                    ..Default::default()
[2515](#2515)                },
[2516](#2516)            )
[2517](#2517)            .unwrap();
[2518](#2518)
[2519](#2519)            assert_eq!(
[2520](#2520)                "[Section1]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n",
[2521](#2521)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2522](#2522)            );
[2523](#2523)        }
[2524](#2524)
[2525](#2525)        {
[2526](#2526)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2527](#2527)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2528](#2528)                &mut buf,
[2529](#2529)                WriteOption {
[2530](#2530)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::CRLF,
[2531](#2531)                    ..Default::default()
[2532](#2532)                },
[2533](#2533)            )
[2534](#2534)            .unwrap();
[2535](#2535)
[2536](#2536)            assert_eq!(
[2537](#2537)                "[Section1]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n\r\n[Section2]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n",
[2538](#2538)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2539](#2539)            );
[2540](#2540)        }
[2541](#2541)
[2542](#2542)        {
[2543](#2543)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2544](#2544)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2545](#2545)                &mut buf,
[2546](#2546)                WriteOption {
[2547](#2547)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::SystemDefault,
[2548](#2548)                    ..Default::default()
[2549](#2549)                },
[2550](#2550)            )
[2551](#2551)            .unwrap();
[2552](#2552)
[2553](#2553)            if cfg!(windows) {
[2554](#2554)                assert_eq!(
[2555](#2555)                    "[Section1]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n\r\n[Section2]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n",
[2556](#2556)                    str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2557](#2557)                );
[2558](#2558)            } else {
[2559](#2559)                assert_eq!(
[2560](#2560)                    "[Section1]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n",
[2561](#2561)                    str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2562](#2562)                );
[2563](#2563)            }
[2564](#2564)        }
[2565](#2565)    }

[2570](#2570)

[2576](#2576)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2577](#2577)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2578](#2578)        ini.with_section(Some("Section2"))
[2579](#2579)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2580](#2580)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2581](#2581)
[2582](#2582)        let mut buf = Vec::new();

[2584](#2584)            &mut buf,
[2585](#2585)            WriteOption {

[2591](#2591)
[2592](#2592)        if cfg!(windows) {
[2594](#2594)            assert_eq!(
[2595](#2595)                "Key1 = Value\r\nKey2 = Value\r\n\r\n[Section1]\r\nKey1 = Value\r\nKey2 = Value\r\n\r\n[Section2]\r\nKey1 = Value\r\nKey2 = Value\r\n",
[2596](#2596)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2597](#2597)            );
[2598](#2598)        } else {
[2599](#2599)            assert_eq!(
[2600](#2600)                "Key1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n\n[Section1]\nKey1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n",
[2601](#2601)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2602](#2602)            );
[2603](#2603)        }

[2606](#2606)    #[test]
[2607](#2607)    fn duplicate_sections() {
[2608](#2608)        let input = r"
[2611](#2611)[Peer]
[2612](#2612)foo = a
[2613](#2613)bar = b
[2614](#2614)
[2615](#2615)[Peer]
[2616](#2616)foo = c
[2617](#2617)bar = d
[2618](#2618)
[2619](#2619)[Peer]
[2620](#2620)foo = e
[2621](#2621)bar = f
[2622](#2622)";
[2623](#2623)
[2624](#2624)        let ini = Ini::load_from_str(input).unwrap();
[2625](#2625)        assert_eq!(3, ini.section_all(Some("Peer")).count());
[2626](#2626)
[2627](#2627)        let mut iter = ini.iter();
[2628](#2628)        let (k0, p0) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2630](#2630)        assert_eq!(None, k0);
[2631](#2631)        assert!(p0.is_empty());
[2632](#2632)        let (k1, p1) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2633](#2633)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k1);
[2634](#2634)        assert_eq!(Some("a"), p1.get("foo"));
[2635](#2635)        assert_eq!(Some("b"), p1.get("bar"));
[2636](#2636)        let (k2, p2) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2637](#2637)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k2);
[2638](#2638)        assert_eq!(Some("c"), p2.get("foo"));
[2639](#2639)        assert_eq!(Some("d"), p2.get("bar"));
[2640](#2640)        let (k3, p3) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2641](#2641)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k3);
[2642](#2642)        assert_eq!(Some("e"), p3.get("foo"));
[2643](#2643)        assert_eq!(Some("f"), p3.get("bar"));
[2644](#2644)
[2645](#2645)        assert_eq!(None, iter.next());
[2646](#2646)    }

[2688](#2688)    #[test]
[2689](#2689)    fn fix_issue63() {
[2690](#2690)        let section = "PHP";
[2691](#2691)        let key = "engine";
[2692](#2692)        let value = "On";
[2693](#2693)        let new_value = "Off";
[2694](#2694)
[2695](#2695)        let mut conf = Ini::new();
[2697](#2697)        conf.with_section(Some(section)).set(key, value);
[2698](#2698)
[2699](#2699)        let v = conf.get_from(Some(section), key).unwrap();
[2701](#2701)        assert_eq!(v, value);
[2702](#2702)
[2703](#2703)        conf.set_to(Some(section), key.to_string(), new_value.to_string());
[2705](#2705)
[2706](#2706)        let v = conf.get_from(Some(section), key).unwrap();
[2708](#2708)        assert_eq!(v, new_value);
[2709](#2709)    }

[2801](#2801)    #[test]
[2802](#2802)    fn escape_str_basics() {
[2803](#2803)        let test_backslash = r"\backslashes\";
[2804](#2804)        let test_nul = "string with \x00nulls\x00 in it";
[2805](#2805)        let test_controls = "|\x07| bell, |\x08| backspace, |\x7f| delete, |\x1b| escape";
[2806](#2806)        let test_whitespace = "\t \r\n";
[2807](#2807)
[2808](#2808)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_backslash, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_backslash);
[2809](#2809)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_nul, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_nul);
[2810](#2810)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_controls, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_controls);
[2811](#2811)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_whitespace, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_whitespace);
[2812](#2812)
[2813](#2813)        for policy in [
[2814](#2814)            EscapePolicy::Basics,
[2815](#2815)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode,
[2816](#2816)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2817](#2817)            EscapePolicy::Reserved,
[2818](#2818)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode,
[2819](#2819)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2820](#2820)            EscapePolicy::Everything,
[2821](#2821)        ] {
[2822](#2822)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_backslash, policy), r"\\backslashes\\");
[2823](#2823)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_nul, policy), r"string with \0nulls\0 in it");
[2824](#2824)            assert_eq!(
[2825](#2825)                escape_str(test_controls, policy),
[2826](#2826)                r"|\a| bell, |\b| backspace, |\x007f| delete, |\x001b| escape"
[2827](#2827)            );
[2828](#2828)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_whitespace, policy), r"\t \r\n");
[2829](#2829)        }
[2830](#2830)    }
[2831](#2831)

[2833](#2833)    fn escape_str_reserved() {
[2834](#2834)        let test_reserved = ":=;#";
[2836](#2836)        let test_punctuation = "!@$%^&*()-_+/?.>,<[]{}``";
[2838](#2838)
[2839](#2839)        for policy in [
[2841](#2841)            EscapePolicy::Nothing,
[2842](#2842)            EscapePolicy::Basics,
[2843](#2843)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode,
[2844](#2844)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2845](#2845)        ] {
[2846](#2846)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_reserved, policy), ":=;#");
[2847](#2847)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_punctuation, policy), test_punctuation);
[2848](#2848)        }
[2849](#2849)
[2850](#2850)        for policy in [
[2852](#2852)            EscapePolicy::Reserved,
[2853](#2853)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2854](#2854)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode,
[2855](#2855)            EscapePolicy::Everything,
[2856](#2856)        ] {
[2857](#2857)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_reserved, policy), r"\:\=\;\#");
[2858](#2858)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_punctuation, policy), "!@$%^&*()-_+/?.>,<[]{}``");
[2859](#2859)        }

[2863](#2863)    fn escape_str_unicode() {
[2864](#2864)        let test_unicode = r"é£∳字✨";
[2869](#2869)        let test_emoji = r"🐱😉";
[2870](#2870)        let test_cjk = r"𠈌𠕇";
[2871](#2871)        let test_high_points = "\u{10ABCD}\u{10FFFF}";
[2872](#2872)
[2873](#2873)        let policy = EscapePolicy::Nothing;
[2874](#2874)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_unicode, policy), test_unicode);
[2875](#2875)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_emoji, policy), test_emoji);
[2876](#2876)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_high_points, policy), test_high_points);
[2877](#2877)
[2878](#2878)        for policy in [EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode, EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode] {
[2881](#2881)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_unicode, policy), r"\x00e9\x00a3\x2233\x5b57\x2728");
[2882](#2882)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_emoji, policy), test_emoji);
[2883](#2883)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_cjk, policy), test_cjk);
[2884](#2884)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_high_points, policy), test_high_points);
[2885](#2885)        }
[2886](#2886)
[2887](#2887)        for policy in [
[2889](#2889)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2890](#2890)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2891](#2891)        ] {
[2892](#2892)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_unicode, policy), r"\x00e9\x00a3\x2233\x5b57\x2728");
[2893](#2893)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_emoji, policy), r"\x1f431\x1f609");
[2894](#2894)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_cjk, policy), r"\x2020c\x20547");
[2895](#2895)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_high_points, policy), r"\x10abcd\x10ffff");
[2896](#2896)        }
[2897](#2897)    }

[2936](#2936)    fn section_setter_chain() {
[2937](#2937)        let mut ini = Ini::new();
[2940](#2940)        let mut section_setter = ini.with_section(Some("section"));
[2941](#2941)
[2942](#2942)        section_setter.set("a", "1").set("b", "2");
[2944](#2944)        section_setter.set("c", "3");
[2946](#2946)
[2947](#2947)        assert_eq!("1", section_setter.get("a").unwrap());
[2948](#2948)        assert_eq!("2", section_setter.get("b").unwrap());
[2949](#2949)        assert_eq!("3", section_setter.get("c").unwrap());
[2950](#2950)
[2951](#2951)        section_setter.set("a", "4").set("b", "5");
[2953](#2953)        section_setter.set("c", "6");
[2954](#2954)
[2955](#2955)        assert_eq!("4", section_setter.get("a").unwrap());
[2956](#2956)        assert_eq!("5", section_setter.get("b").unwrap());
[2957](#2957)        assert_eq!("6", section_setter.get("c").unwrap());
[2958](#2958)
[2959](#2959)        section_setter.delete(&"a").delete(&"b");
[2961](#2961)        section_setter.delete(&"c");
[2962](#2962)
[2963](#2963)        assert!(section_setter.get("a").is_none());
[2964](#2964)        assert!(section_setter.get("b").is_none());
[2965](#2965)        assert!(section_setter.get("c").is_none());
[2966](#2966)    }

[2969](#2969)    fn parse_enabled_indented_mutiline_value() {
[2970](#2970)        let input = "
[2971](#2971)[Foo]
[2972](#2972)bar =
[2973](#2973)    u
[2974](#2974)    v
[2975](#2975)
[2976](#2976)baz = w
[2977](#2977)  x # intentional trailing whitespace below
[2978](#2978)   y
[2979](#2979)
[2980](#2980) z #2
[2981](#2981)bla = a
[2982](#2982)";
[2983](#2983)
[2984](#2984)        let opt = Ini::load_from_str_opt(
[2985](#2985)            input,
[2986](#2986)            ParseOption {
[2987](#2987)                enabled_indented_mutiline_value: true,
[2988](#2988)                ..ParseOption::default()
[2989](#2989)            },
[2990](#2990)        )
[2991](#2991)        .unwrap();
[2992](#2992)        let sec = opt.section(Some("Foo")).unwrap();
[2993](#2993)        let mut iterator = sec.iter();
[2994](#2994)        let bar = iterator.next().unwrap().1;
[2995](#2995)        let baz = iterator.next().unwrap().1;
[2996](#2996)        let bla = iterator.next().unwrap().1;
[2997](#2997)        assert!(iterator.next().is_none());
[2998](#2998)        assert_eq!(bar, "u\nv");
[2999](#2999)        if cfg!(feature = "inline-comment") {
[3000](#3000)            assert_eq!(baz, "w\nx\ny\n\nz");
[3001](#3001)        } else {
[3002](#3002)            assert_eq!(baz, "w\nx # intentional trailing whitespace below\ny\n\nz #2");
[3003](#3003)        }
[3004](#3004)        assert_eq!(bla, "a");
[3005](#3005)    }

[3126](#3126)    fn section_after_whitespace_bug_reproduction() {
[3127](#3127)        let input = "[SectionA]\nKey1=Value1\n\n  [SectionB]\n  Key2=Value2";
[3128](#3128)
[3129](#3129)        let data_default = Ini::load_from_str(input).unwrap();
[3131](#3131)
[3132](#3132)        assert!(data_default.section(Some("SectionA")).is_some());
[3134](#3134)        assert!(data_default.section(Some("SectionB")).is_some());
[3135](#3135)
[3136](#3136)        let section_a = data_default.section(Some("SectionA")).unwrap();
[3137](#3137)        let section_b = data_default.section(Some("SectionB")).unwrap();
[3138](#3138)
[3139](#3139)        assert_eq!(section_a.get("Key1"), Some("Value1"));
[3140](#3140)        assert_eq!(section_b.get("Key2"), Some("Value2"));
[3141](#3141)
[3142](#3142)        let mut opts = ParseOption::default();
[3144](#3144)        opts.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace = true;
[3145](#3145)        let data_preserve = Ini::load_from_str_opt(input, opts).unwrap();
[3146](#3146)
[3147](#3147)        assert!(data_preserve.section(Some("SectionA")).is_some());
[3149](#3149)        assert!(data_preserve.section(Some("SectionB")).is_some());
[3150](#3150)
[3151](#3151)        let section_a_preserve = data_preserve.section(Some("SectionA")).unwrap();
[3152](#3152)        let section_b_preserve = data_preserve.section(Some("SectionB")).unwrap();
[3153](#3153)
[3154](#3154)        assert_eq!(section_a_preserve.get("Key1"), Some("Value1"));
[3155](#3155)        assert_eq!(section_b_preserve.get("  Key2"), Some("Value2"));
[3157](#3157)    }
