# Ini in ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/0.21.3/ini/struct.Ini.html

`pub struct Ini { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Ini struct

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Create an instance

```
7fn main() {
8    let mut conf = Ini::new();
9    conf.with_section(None::<String>).set("encoding", "utf-8");
10    conf.with_section(Some("User"))
11        .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
12        .set("value", "Pi");
13    conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
14        .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
15        .set("location", "Guangzhou=world\x0ahahaha");
16
17    conf.section_mut(Some("Library")).unwrap().insert("seats", "42");
18
19    println!("---------------------------------------");
20    println!("Writing to file {:?}\n", CONF_FILE_NAME);
21    conf.write_to(&mut stdout()).unwrap();
22
23    conf.write_to_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
24
25    println!("----------------------------------------");
26    println!("Reading from file {:?}", CONF_FILE_NAME);
27    let i = Ini::load_from_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
28
29    println!("Iterating");
30    let general_section_name = "__General__";
31    for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
32        let section_name = sec.as_ref().unwrap_or(&general_section_name);
33        println!("-- Section: {:?} begins", section_name);
34        for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
35            println!("{}: {:?}", k, v);
36        }
37    }
38    println!();
39
40    let section = i.section(Some("User")).unwrap();
41    println!("name={}", section.get("name").unwrap());
42    println!("conf[User][name]={}", &i["User"]["name"]);
43    println!("General Section: {:?}", i.general_section());
44}
```

```
7fn main() {
8    let mut conf = Ini::new();
9    conf.with_section(None::<String>).set("encoding", "utf-8");
10    conf.with_section(Some("User"))
11        .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
12        .set("value", "Pi");
13    conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
14        .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
15        .set("location", "Guangzhou=world\x0ahahaha");
16
17    conf.section_mut(Some("Library")).unwrap().insert("seats", "42");
18
19    println!("---------------------------------------");
20    println!("Writing to file {:?}\n", CONF_FILE_NAME);
21    conf.write_to(&mut stdout()).unwrap();
22
23    conf.write_to_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
24
25    println!("----------------------------------------");
26    println!("Reading from file {:?}", CONF_FILE_NAME);
27    let i = Ini::load_from_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
28
29    println!("Iterating");
30    let general_section_name = "__General__";
31    for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
32        let section_name = sec.as_ref().unwrap_or(&general_section_name);
33        println!("-- Section: {:?} begins", section_name);
34        for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
35            println!("{}: {:?}", k, v);
36        }
37    }
38    println!();

40    let section = i.section(Some("User")).unwrap();
41    println!("name={}", section.get("name").unwrap());
42    println!("conf[User][name]={}", &i["User"]["name"]);

# ParseOption in ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/0.21.3/ini/struct.ParseOption.html

```
pub struct ParseOption {
    pub enabled_quote:
```
[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub enabled_escape: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub enabled_indented_mutiline_value: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
}## Expand description

Parsing configuration

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled_quote)

`enabled_quote: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Allow quote (`"` or `'`) in value
For example

```
[Section]
Key1="Quoted value"
Key2='Single Quote' with extra value
```
In this example, Value of `Key1` is `Quoted value`,
and value of `Key2` is `Single Quote with extra value`
if `enabled_quote` is set to `true`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled_escape)

`enabled_escape: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Interpret `\` as an escape character
For example

```
[Section]
Key1=C:\Windows
```
If `enabled_escape` is true, then the value of `Key` will become `C:Windows` (`\W` equals to `W`).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled_indented_mutiline_value)

`enabled_indented_mutiline_value: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Enables values that span lines

```
[Section]
foo=
  b
  c
```
[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace)

`enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)Preserve key leading whitespace

```
[services my-services]
dynamodb=
  endpoint_url=http://localhost:8000
```
The leading whitespace in key `  endpoint_url` will be preserved if `enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace` is set to `true`.

11        .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
12        .set("value", "Pi");
13    conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
14        .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
15        .set("location", "Guangzhou=world\x0ahahaha");
16
17    conf.section_mut(Some("Library")).unwrap().insert("seats", "42");
18
19    println!("---------------------------------------");
20    println!("Writing to file {:?}\n", CONF_FILE_NAME);
21    conf.write_to(&mut stdout()).unwrap();
22
23    conf.write_to_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
24
25    println!("----------------------------------------");
26    println!("Reading from file {:?}", CONF_FILE_NAME);
27    let i = Ini::load_from_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
28
29    println!("Iterating");
30    let general_section_name = "__General__";
31    for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
32        let section_name = sec.as_ref().unwrap_or(&general_section_name);
33        println!("-- Section: {:?} begins", section_name);
34        for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
35            println!("{}: {:?}", k, v);
36        }
37    }
38    println!();
39
40    let section = i.section(Some("User")).unwrap();
41    println!("name={}", section.get("name").unwrap());
42    println!("conf[User][name]={}", &i["User"]["name"]);
43    println!("General Section: {:?}", i.general_section());
44}
```
Get all values associate with the key

Set (replace) key-value pair in this section (all with the same name)

```
7fn main() {
8    let mut conf = Ini::new();
9    conf.with_section(None::<String>).set("encoding", "utf-8");
10    conf.with_section(Some("User"))
11        .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
12        .set("value", "Pi");
13    conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
14        .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
15        .set("location", "Guangzhou=world\x0ahahaha");
16
17    conf.section_mut(Some("Library")).unwrap().insert("seats", "42");
18
19    println!("---------------------------------------");
20    println!("Writing to file {:?}\n", CONF_FILE_NAME);
21    conf.write_to(&mut stdout()).unwrap();
22
23    conf.write_to_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
24
25    println!("----------------------------------------");
26    println!("Reading from file {:?}", CONF_FILE_NAME);
27    let i = Ini::load_from_file(CONF_FILE_NAME).unwrap();
28
29    println!("Iterating");
30    let general_section_name = "__General__";
31    for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
32        let section_name = sec.as_ref().unwrap_or(&general_section_name);
33        println!("-- Section: {:?} begins", section_name);
34        for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
35            println!("{}: {:?}", k, v);
36        }
37    }
38    println!();
39
40    let section = i.section(Some("User")).unwrap();
41    println!("name={}", section.get("name").unwrap());
42    println!("conf[User][name]={}", &i["User"]["name"]);
43    println!("General Section: {:?}", i.general_section());
44}
```

# EscapePolicy in ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/0.21.3/ini/enum.EscapePolicy.html

```
pub enum EscapePolicy {
    Nothing,
    Basics,
    BasicsUnicode,
    BasicsUnicodeExtended,
    Reserved,
    ReservedUnicode,
    ReservedUnicodeExtended,
    Everything,
}
```
## Expand description

Policies for escaping logic

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Nothing)

### Nothing

Escape absolutely nothing (dangerous)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Basics)

### Basics

Only escape the most necessary things. This means backslashes, control characters (codepoints U+0000 to U+001F), and delete (U+007F). Quotes (single or double) are not escaped.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BasicsUnicode)

### BasicsUnicode

Escape basics and non-ASCII characters in the [Basic Multilingual Plane](https://www.compart.com/en/unicode/plane)
(i.e. between U+007F - U+FFFF)
Codepoints above U+FFFF, e.g. ‘🐱’ U+1F431 “CAT FACE” will *not* be escaped!

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BasicsUnicodeExtended)

### BasicsUnicodeExtended

Escape basics and all non-ASCII characters, including codepoints above U+FFFF. This will escape emoji - if you want them to remain raw, use BasicsUnicode instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Reserved)

### Reserved

Escape reserved symbols. This includes everything in EscapePolicy::Basics, plus the comment characters ‘;’ and ‘#’ and the key/value-separating characters ‘=’ and ‘:’.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ReservedUnicode)

### ReservedUnicode

Escape reserved symbols and non-ASCII characters in the BMP.
Codepoints above U+FFFF, e.g. ‘🐱’ U+1F431 “CAT FACE” will *not* be escaped!

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ReservedUnicodeExtended)

### ReservedUnicodeExtended

Escape reserved symbols and all non-ASCII characters, including codepoints above U+FFFF.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Everything)

### Everything

Escape everything that some INI implementations assume

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

pub enum LineSeparator {

    CR,
    CRLF,

```
## Expand description

Newline style

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SystemDefault)

### SystemDefault

System-dependent line separator

On UNIX system, uses “\n” On Windows system, uses “\r\n”

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CR)

### CR

Uses “\n” as new line separator

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CRLF)

### CRLF

Uses “\r\n” as new line separator

# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini/latest/ini/

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```

# cfg-if

A macro to ergonomically define an item depending on a large number of #[cfg] parameters. Structured like an if-else chain, the first matching branch is the item that gets emitted.

 = "1.0"
```

cfg_if!
```

# ordered-multimap 0.7.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ordered-multimap/^0.7

# ordered-multimap-rs

Currently, this crate contains a single type `ListOrderedMultimap`. This is a multimap meaning that
multiple values can be associated with a given key, but it also maintains insertion order across all
keys and values.

## Performance

Basic benchmarks show that the performance of this crate is on par with that of the
[multimap](https://crates.io/crates/multimap) crate which does not maintain insertion order.

## Features

- `std`(default) enables usage of the standard library. Disabling this features allows this crate to be used in- `no_std`environments.
- `serde`for (de)serialization.

## TODO

It is planned that a corresponding `SetOrderedMultimap` will also be included in this crate which
will provide the same insertion order guarantees, but the set of values associated to a given key
will be an actual set instead of a list.

## License

Licensed under MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT) or [http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)).

## Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you shall be licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# unicase 2.9.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicase/^2.6

# unicase

Compare strings when case is not important (using Unicode Case-folding).

```
// ignore ASCII case
let a = new;
let b = new;
assert_eq!;
// using unicode case-folding
let c = new
let d = new;
assert_eq!;
```

# rust-ini 0.21.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.21.2

# INI in Rust

[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".

This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).

```
[]
 = "0.21"
```
## Usage

- Create a Ini configuration file.

```
extern crate ini;
use Ini;
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`

```
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green

# rust-ini 0.21.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.21.1

# INI in Rust

[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".

This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).

```
[]
 = "0.21"
```
## Usage

- Create a Ini configuration file.

```
extern crate ini;
use Ini;
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`

```
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green
unicode=Raspberry\x6811\x8393
[Book]
name=Rust cool
```
- Read from file `conf.ini`

```
use Ini;
```
- More details could be found in `examples`.

# INI in Rust

[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".

This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).

```
[]
 = "0.19"
```
## Usage

- Create a Ini configuration file.

```
extern crate ini;
use Ini;
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`

```
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green
unicode=Raspberry\x6811\x8393
[Book]
name=Rust cool
```
- Read from file `conf.ini`

```
use Ini;
```
- More details could be found in `examples`.

# rust-ini 0.19.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.19.0

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
.set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
.set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
.set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
.set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
println!("{}:{}", k, v);
}
}
```

---

# rust-ini 0.14.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/0.14.0

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User".to_owned()))
.set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
.set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library".to_owned()))
.set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
.set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
println!("Section: {:?}", *sec);
for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
println!("{}:{}", *k, *v);
}
}
```

    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
   println!("Section: {:?}", *sec);
   for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
       println!("{}:{}", *k, *v);
   }
}
```

# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rust-ini

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Ini](https://docs.rs/struct.Ini.html)
- Ini struct
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseError.html)- Error
- Parse error
- [Parse](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseOption.html)- Option
- Parsing configuration
- [Properties](https://docs.rs/struct.Properties.html)
- Properties type (key-value pairs)
- [Properties](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertiesIntoIter.html)- Into - Iter
- [Property](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyIter.html)- Iter
- [Property](https://docs.rs/struct.PropertyIterMut.html)- Iter - Mut
- Iterator for traversing sections
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionIntoIter.html)- Into - Iter
- Iterator for traversing sections
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionIter.html)- Iter
- Iterator for traversing sections
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionIterMut.html)- Iter - Mut
- Iterator for traversing sections
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionOccupiedEntry.html)- Occupied - Entry
- A view into a occupied entry in a `Ini`
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionSetter.html)- Setter
- A setter which could be used to set key-value pair in a specified section
- [Section](https://docs.rs/struct.SectionVacantEntry.html)- Vacant - Entry
- A view into a vacant entry in a `Ini`
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteOption.html)- Option
- Writing configuration

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Error while parsing an INI document
- [Escape](https://docs.rs/enum.EscapePolicy.html)- Policy
- Policies for escaping logic
- [Line](https://docs.rs/enum.LineSeparator.html)- Separator
- Newline style
- [Section](https://docs.rs/enum.SectionEntry.html)- Entry
- A view into an `Ini`, which may either be vacant or occupied.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Property](https://docs.rs/type.PropertyKey.html)- Key
- Internal storage of property’s key
- [Section](https://docs.rs/type.SectionKey.html)- Key
- Internal storage of section’s key

# rust-ini 0.21.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/latest/source/README.md

```
[![Build & Test](https://github.com/zonyitoo/rust-ini/actions/workflows/build-and-test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/zonyitoo/rust-ini/actions/workflows/build-and-test.yml)
[![crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/rust-ini.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/rust-ini)
[![doc.rs](https://docs.rs/rust-ini/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/rust-ini)
[INI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/INI_file) is an informal standard for configuration files for some platforms or software. INI files are simple text files with a basic structure composed of "sections" and "properties".
This is an INI file parser in [Rust](http://www.rust-lang.org/).
```toml
[dependencies]
rust-ini = "0.21"
```
*
```rust
extern crate ini;
use ini::Ini;
fn main() {
}
```
Then you will get `conf.ini`
```ini
encoding=utf-8
[User]
given_name=Tommy
family_name=Green
unicode=Raspberry\x6811\x8393
[Book]
name=Rust cool
```
*
```rust
use ini::Ini;
fn main() {
}
```

# cfg-if

A macro to ergonomically define an item depending on a large number of #[cfg] parameters. Structured like an if-else chain, the first matching branch is the item that gets emitted.

 = "1.0"
```

cfg_if!
```

# cfg_if - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cfg-if/1.0.4/target-redirect/cfg_if/

## Expand description

A macro for defining `#[cfg]` if-else statements.

The macro provided by this crate, `cfg_if`, is similar to the `if/elif` C
preprocessor macro by allowing definition of a cascade of `#[cfg]` cases,
emitting the implementation which matches first.

This allows you to conveniently provide a long list `#[cfg]`’d blocks of code
without having to rewrite each clause multiple times.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
cfg_if::cfg_if! {
    if #[cfg(unix)] {
        fn foo() { /* unix specific functionality */ }
    } else if #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")] {
        fn foo() { /* non-unix, 32-bit functionality */ }
    } else {
        fn foo() { /* fallback implementation */ }
    }
}
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [cfg_if](https://docs.rs/macro.cfg_if.html)
- The main macro provided by this crate. See crate documentation for more information.

---

# cfg_if in cfg_if - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cfg-if/^1.0/macro.cfg_if.html

```
macro_rules! cfg_if {
    (
        if #[cfg( $($i_meta:tt)+ )] { $( $i_tokens:tt )* }
        $(
            else if #[cfg( $($ei_meta:tt)+ )] { $( $ei_tokens:tt )* }
        )*
        $(
            else { $( $e_tokens:tt )* }
        )?
    ) => { ... };
    (@__items ( $( ($($_:tt)*) , )* ) ; ) => { ... };
    (
        @__items ( $( ($($no:tt)+) , )* ) ;
        (( $( $($yes:tt)+ )? ) ( $( $tokens:tt )* )),
        $( $rest:tt , )*
    ) => { ... };
    (@__temp_group $( $tokens:tt )* ) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

The main macro provided by this crate. See crate documentation for more information.

# ordered-multimap 0.7.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/ordered-multimap/0.7.3

# ordered-multimap-rs

Currently, this crate contains a single type `ListOrderedMultimap`. This is a multimap meaning that
multiple values can be associated with a given key, but it also maintains insertion order across all
keys and values.

## Performance

Basic benchmarks show that the performance of this crate is on par with that of the
[multimap](https://crates.io/crates/multimap) crate which does not maintain insertion order.

## Features

- `std`(default) enables usage of the standard library. Disabling this features allows this crate to be used in- `no_std`environments.
- `serde`for (de)serialization.

## TODO

It is planned that a corresponding `SetOrderedMultimap` will also be included in this crate which
will provide the same insertion order guarantees, but the set of values associated to a given key
will be an actual set instead of a list.

## License

Licensed under MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT) or [http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT](http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)).

## Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you shall be licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# hashbrown - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/hashbrown/^0.14.0/

## Expand description

This crate is a Rust port of Google’s high-performance [SwissTable](https://abseil.io/blog/20180927-swisstables) hash
map, adapted to make it a drop-in replacement for Rust’s standard `HashMap`
and `HashSet` types.

The original C++ version of [SwissTable](https://abseil.io/blog/20180927-swisstables) can be found [here](https://github.com/abseil/abseil-cpp/blob/master/absl/container/internal/raw_hash_set.h), and this
[CppCon talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncHmEUmJZf4) gives an overview of how the algorithm works.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- A hash map implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.
- A hash set implemented as a`HashMap`where the value is`()`.
- A hash table implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.
- Experimental and unsafe`RawTable`API. This module is only available if the`raw`feature is enabled.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- A hash map implemented with quadratic probing and SIMD lookup.
- A hash set implemented as a`HashMap`where the value is`()`.
- Low-level hash table with explicit hashing.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- The error type for`try_reserve`methods.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- Key equivalence trait.

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/^1/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any - `docsrs`
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

## Derive Macros[§](https://docs.rs#derives)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Deserialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/derive.Serialize.html)- `derive`
- Derive macro available if serde is built with `features = ["derive"]`.

---

# coverage_helper - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/coverage-helper/^0.2.0/

## Expand description

**Note: This crate is now deprecated in favor of the pattern that is  recommended in the cargo-llvm-cov documentation.**

If you want to ignore all

`#[test]`-related code, you can use module-level`#[coverage(off)]`attribute:`#![cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, feature(coverage_attribute))] #[cfg(test)] #[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))] mod tests { // ... }`cargo-llvm-cov excludes code contained in the directory named

`tests`from the report by default, so you can also use it instead of`#[coverage(off)]`attribute.

Helper for [https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/issues/123](https://github.com/taiki-e/cargo-llvm-cov/issues/123).

**Note:** coverage-helper 0.2 supports `#[coverage(off)]`.
See coverage-helper 0.1 for versions that support `#[no_coverage]`.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dev-dependencies]
coverage-helper = "0.2"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use coverage_helper::test;
#[test]
fn my_test() {
    // ...
}
```
Expanded to:

```
#[cfg_attr(all(coverage_nightly, test), coverage(off))]
#[::core::prelude::v1::test]
fn my_test() {
    // ...
}
```
## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [test](https://docs.rs/attr.test.html)- Deprecated

---

# serde_test - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_test/^1.0.144/

## Expand description

This crate provides a convenient concise way to write unit tests for
implementations of [ Serialize](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serialize.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/de/trait.Deserialize.html)

`Deserialize`The `Serialize` impl for a value can be characterized by the sequence of
[ Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html) calls that are made in the course of serializing the value,
so

`serde_test` provides a [abstraction which corresponds roughly to](https://docs.rs/enum.Token.html)

`Token``Serializer` method calls. There is an [function to test that a value serializes to a particular sequence of method calls, an](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_ser_tokens.html)

`assert_ser_tokens`[function to test that a value can be deserialized from a particular sequence of method calls, and an](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_de_tokens.html)

`assert_de_tokens`[function to test both directions. There are also functions to test expected failure conditions.](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_tokens.html)

`assert_tokens`Here is an example from the [ linked-hash-map](https://github.com/contain-rs/linked-hash-map) crate.

```
use linked_hash_map::LinkedHashMap;
use serde_test::{assert_tokens, Token};
#[test]
fn test_ser_de_empty() {
    let map = LinkedHashMap::<char, u32>::new();
    assert_tokens(
        &map,
        &[
            Token::Map { len: Some(0) },
            Token::MapEnd,
        ],
    );
}
#[test]
fn test_ser_de() {
    let mut map = LinkedHashMap::new();
    map.insert('b', 20);
    map.insert('a', 10);
    map.insert('c', 30);
    assert_tokens(
        &map,
        &[
            Token::Map { len: Some(3) },
            Token::Char('b'),
            Token::I32(20),
            Token::Char('a'),
            Token::I32(10),
            Token::Char('c'),
            Token::I32(30),
            Token::MapEnd,
        ],
    );
}
```

- [assert_](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_de_tokens_error.html)- de_ - tokens_ - error
- Asserts that the given `tokens`yield`error`when deserializing.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_ser_tokens.html)- ser_ - tokens
- Asserts that `value`serializes to the given`tokens`.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_ser_tokens_error.html)- ser_ - tokens_ - error
- Asserts that `value`serializes to the given`tokens`, and then yields`error`.
- [assert_](https://docs.rs/fn.assert_tokens.html)- tokens
- Runs both `assert_ser_tokens`and`assert_de_tokens`.

# unicase 2.9.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicase/2.9.0

# unicase

Compare strings when case is not important (using Unicode Case-folding).

```
// ignore ASCII case
let a = new;
let b = new;
assert_eq!;
// using unicode case-folding
let c = new
let d = new;
assert_eq!;
```

# unicase - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/unicase/2.9.0/target-redirect/unicase/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#unicase)UniCase

UniCase provides a way of specifying strings that are case-insensitive.

UniCase supports full [Unicode case
folding](https://www.w3.org/International/wiki/Case_folding). It can also
utilize faster ASCII case comparisons, if both strings are ASCII.

Using the `UniCase::new()` constructor will check the string to see if it
is all ASCII. When a `UniCase` is compared against another, if both are
ASCII, it will use the faster comparison.

There also exists the `Ascii` type in this crate, which will always assume
to use the ASCII case comparisons, if the encoding is already known.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use unicase::UniCase;
let a = UniCase::new("Maße");
let b = UniCase::new("MASSE");
let c = UniCase::new("mase");
assert_eq!(a, b);
assert!(b != c);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#ascii)Ascii

```
use unicase::Ascii;
let a = Ascii::new("foobar");
let b = Ascii::new("FoObAr");
assert_eq!(a, b);
```

# eq in unicase - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicase/^2.6/fn.eq.html

## Expand description

Compare two string-like types for case-less equality, using unicode folding.

Equivalent to `UniCase::new(left) == UniCase::new(right)`.

Note: This will perform a scan for ASCII characters before doing the
the comparison. See `UniCase` for more information.

---

# eq_ascii in unicase - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/unicase/^2.6/fn.eq_ascii.html

## Expand description

Compare two string-like types for case-less equality, ignoring ASCII case.

Equivalent to `Ascii::new(left) == Ascii::new(right)`.

---

# ini - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rust-ini/latest/target-redirect/ini/index.html

## Expand description

Ini parser for Rust

```
use ini::Ini;
let mut conf = Ini::new();
conf.with_section(Some("User"))
    .set("name", "Raspberry树莓")
    .set("value", "Pi");
conf.with_section(Some("Library"))
    .set("name", "Sun Yat-sen U")
    .set("location", "Guangzhou=world");
conf.write_to_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
let i = Ini::load_from_file("conf.ini").unwrap();
for (sec, prop) in i.iter() {
    println!("Section: {:?}", sec);
    for (k, v) in prop.iter() {
        println!("{}:{}", k, v);
    }
}
```

[95](#95)        self != EscapePolicy::Nothing
[96](#96)    }
[97](#97)
[98](#98)    fn escape_reserved(self) -> bool {
[99](#99)        matches!(
[100](#100)            self,
[101](#101)            EscapePolicy::Reserved
[102](#102)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode
[103](#103)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended
[104](#104)                | EscapePolicy::Everything
[105](#105)        )
[106](#106)    }

[108](#108)    fn escape_unicode(self) -> bool {
[109](#109)        matches!(
[110](#110)            self,
[111](#111)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode
[112](#112)                | EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended
[113](#113)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode
[114](#114)                | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended
[115](#115)                | EscapePolicy::Everything
[116](#116)        )
[117](#117)    }

[120](#120)        matches!(
[121](#121)            self,
[122](#122)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended | EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended | EscapePolicy::Everything
[123](#123)        )
[124](#124)    }
[125](#125)
[126](#126)    pub fn should_escape(self, c: char) -> bool {
[129](#129)        match c {
[130](#130)            '\\' | '\x00'..='\x1f' | '\x7f' => self.escape_basics(),
[133](#133)            ';' | '#' | '=' | ':' => self.escape_reserved(),
[134](#134)            '\u{0080}'..='\u{FFFF}' => self.escape_unicode(),
[135](#135)            '\u{10000}'..='\u{10FFFF}' => self.escape_unicode_extended(),
[136](#136)            _ => false,
[137](#137)        }
[138](#138)    }
[139](#139)}
[140](#140)
[141](#141)fn escape_str(s: &str, policy: EscapePolicy) -> String {
[158](#158)    let mut escaped: String = String::with_capacity(s.len());
[159](#159)    for c in s.chars() {
[160](#160)        if !policy.should_escape(c) {
[163](#163)            escaped.push(c);
[164](#164)            continue;
[165](#165)        }
[166](#166)
[167](#167)        match c {
[168](#168)            '\\' => escaped.push_str("\\\\"),
[169](#169)            '\0' => escaped.push_str("\\0"),
[170](#170)            '\x01'..='\x06' | '\x0e'..='\x1f' | '\x7f'..='\u{00ff}' => {
[171](#171)                escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:04x}", c as isize)[..])
[172](#172)            }
[173](#173)            '\x07' => escaped.push_str("\\a"),
[174](#174)            '\x08' => escaped.push_str("\\b"),
[175](#175)            '\x0c' => escaped.push_str("\\f"),
[176](#176)            '\x0b' => escaped.push_str("\\v"),
[177](#177)            '\n' => escaped.push_str("\\n"),
[178](#178)            '\t' => escaped.push_str("\\t"),
[179](#179)            '\r' => escaped.push_str("\\r"),
[180](#180)            '\u{0080}'..='\u{FFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:04x}", c as isize)[..]),
[181](#181)            '\u{10000}'..='\u{FFFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:05x}", c as isize)[..]),
[183](#183)            '\u{100000}'..='\u{10FFFF}' => escaped.push_str(&format!("\\x{:06x}", c as isize)[..]),
[184](#184)            _ => {
[185](#185)                escaped.push('\\');
[186](#186)                escaped.push(c);
[187](#187)            }
[188](#188)        }
[189](#189)    }
[190](#190)    escaped
[191](#191)}

[391](#391)    pub fn add<'b, K, V>(&'b mut self, key: K, value: V) -> &'b mut SectionSetter<'a>
[393](#393)    where
[394](#394)        K: Into<String>,
[395](#395)        V: Into<String>,
[396](#396)        'a: 'b,
[397](#397)    {
[398](#398)        self.ini
[399](#399)            .entry(self.section_name.clone())
[400](#400)            .or_insert_with(Default::default)
[401](#401)            .append(key, value);
[402](#402)
[403](#403)        self
[404](#404)    }
[405](#405)
[406](#406)    pub fn delete<'b, K>(&'b mut self, key: &K) -> &'b mut SectionSetter<'a>
[408](#408)    where
[409](#409)        K: AsRef<str>,
[410](#410)        'a: 'b,
[411](#411)    {
[412](#412)        for prop in self.ini.section_all_mut(self.section_name.as_ref()) {
[413](#413)            prop.remove(key);
[414](#414)        }
[415](#415)
[416](#416)        self
[417](#417)    }
[418](#418)
[419](#419)    pub fn get<K: AsRef<str>>(&'a self, key: K) -> Option<&'a str> {
[421](#421)        self.ini
[422](#422)            .section(self.section_name.as_ref())
[423](#423)            .and_then(|prop| prop.get(key))
[424](#424)            .map(AsRef::as_ref)
[425](#425)    }
[426](#426)}

[658](#658)pub enum SectionEntry<'a> {
[660](#660)    Vacant(SectionVacantEntry<'a>),

[662](#662)}
[663](#663)
[664](#664)impl<'a> SectionEntry<'a> {
[665](#665)    pub fn or_insert(self, properties: Properties) -> &'a mut Properties {
[667](#667)        match self {
[668](#668)            SectionEntry::Occupied(e) => e.into_mut(),
[669](#669)            SectionEntry::Vacant(e) => e.insert(properties),
[670](#670)        }
[671](#671)    }
[672](#672)
[673](#673)    pub fn or_insert_with<F: FnOnce() -> Properties>(self, default: F) -> &'a mut Properties {
[675](#675)        match self {
[676](#676)            SectionEntry::Occupied(e) => e.into_mut(),
[677](#677)            SectionEntry::Vacant(e) => e.insert(default()),
[678](#678)        }
[679](#679)    }
[680](#680)}
[681](#681)
[682](#682)impl<'a> From<Entry<'a, SectionKey, Properties>> for SectionEntry<'a> {
[683](#683)    fn from(e: Entry<'a, SectionKey, Properties>) -> SectionEntry<'a> {
[684](#684)        match e {
[685](#685)            Entry::Occupied(inner) => SectionEntry::Occupied(SectionOccupiedEntry { inner }),
[686](#686)            Entry::Vacant(inner) => SectionEntry::Vacant(SectionVacantEntry { inner }),
[687](#687)        }
[688](#688)    }

[920](#920)    }
[921](#921)
[922](#922)    pub fn write_to_file_policy<P: AsRef<Path>>(&self, filename: P, policy: EscapePolicy) -> io::Result<()> {
[924](#924)        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
[925](#925)            .write(true)
[926](#926)            .truncate(true)
[927](#927)            .create(true)
[928](#928)            .open(filename.as_ref())?;
[929](#929)        self.write_to_policy(&mut file, policy)
[930](#930)    }
[931](#931)
[932](#932)    pub fn write_to_file_opt<P: AsRef<Path>>(&self, filename: P, opt: WriteOption) -> io::Result<()> {
[934](#934)        let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
[935](#935)            .write(true)
[936](#936)            .truncate(true)
[937](#937)            .create(true)
[938](#938)            .open(filename.as_ref())?;
[939](#939)        self.write_to_opt(&mut file, opt)
[940](#940)    }
[941](#941)
[942](#942)    pub fn write_to<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W) -> io::Result<()> {
[944](#944)        self.write_to_opt(writer, Default::default())
[945](#945)    }
[946](#946)
[947](#947)    pub fn write_to_policy<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W, policy: EscapePolicy) -> io::Result<()> {
[949](#949)        self.write_to_opt(
[950](#950)            writer,
[951](#951)            WriteOption {
[952](#952)                escape_policy: policy,
[953](#953)                ..Default::default()
[954](#954)            },
[955](#955)        )
[956](#956)    }
[957](#957)
[958](#958)    pub fn write_to_opt<W: Write>(&self, writer: &mut W, opt: WriteOption) -> io::Result<()> {
[960](#960)        let mut firstline = true;
[961](#961)
[962](#962)        for (section, props) in &self.sections {
[963](#963)            if !props.data.is_empty() {
[964](#964)                if firstline {
[965](#965)                    firstline = false;
[966](#966)                } else {
[967](#967)                    writer.write_all(opt.line_separator.as_str().as_bytes())?;
[969](#969)                }
[970](#970)            }
[971](#971)
[972](#972)            if let Some(ref section) = *section {
[973](#973)                write!(
[974](#974)                    writer,
[975](#975)                    "[{}]{}",
[976](#976)                    escape_str(§ion[..], opt.escape_policy),
[977](#977)                    opt.line_separator
[978](#978)                )?;
[979](#979)            }
[980](#980)            for (k, v) in props.iter() {
[981](#981)                let k_str = escape_str(k, opt.escape_policy);
[982](#982)                let v_str = escape_str(v, opt.escape_policy);
[983](#983)                write!(writer, "{}{}{}{}", k_str, opt.kv_separator, v_str, opt.line_separator)?;
[984](#984)            }
[985](#985)        }
[986](#986)        Ok(())

[1230](#1230)pub enum Error {

[1232](#1232)    Parse(ParseError),

[1235](#1235)impl Display for Error {

[1237](#1237)        match *self {
[1238](#1238)            Error::Io(ref err) => err.fmt(f),
[1239](#1239)            Error::Parse(ref err) => err.fmt(f),
[1240](#1240)        }

[1244](#1244)impl error::Error for Error {
[1245](#1245)    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn error::Error + 'static)> {
[1246](#1246)        match *self {
[1247](#1247)            Error::Io(ref err) => err.source(),
[1248](#1248)            Error::Parse(ref err) => err.source(),
[1249](#1249)        }
[1250](#1250)    }
[1251](#1251)}
[1252](#1252)
[1253](#1253)impl From<io::Error> for Error {
[1254](#1254)    fn from(err: io::Error) -> Self {
[1255](#1255)        Error::Io(err)
[1256](#1256)    }
[1257](#1257)}
[1258](#1258)
[1259](#1259)impl<'a> Parser<'a> {
[1260](#1260)    pub fn new(rdr: Chars<'a>, opt: ParseOption) -> Parser<'a> {
[1262](#1262)        let mut p = Parser {
[1263](#1263)            ch: None,
[1264](#1264)            line: 0,
[1265](#1265)            col: 0,
[1266](#1266)            rdr,
[1267](#1267)            opt,
[1268](#1268)        };
[1269](#1269)        p.bump();
[1270](#1270)        p
[1271](#1271)    }
[1272](#1272)
[1273](#1273)    fn bump(&mut self) {
[1274](#1274)        self.ch = self.rdr.next();
[1275](#1275)        match self.ch {
[1276](#1276)            Some('\n') => {
[1277](#1277)                self.line += 1;
[1278](#1278)                self.col = 0;
[1279](#1279)            }
[1280](#1280)            Some(..) => {
[1281](#1281)                self.col += 1;
[1282](#1282)            }
[1283](#1283)            None => {}
[1284](#1284)        }
[1285](#1285)    }
[1286](#1286)
[1287](#1287)    #[cold]
[1288](#1288)    #[inline(never)]
[1289](#1289)    fn error<U, M: Into<Cow<'static, str>>>(&self, msg: M) -> Result<U, ParseError> {
[1290](#1290)        Err(ParseError {
[1291](#1291)            line: self.line + 1,
[1292](#1292)            col: self.col + 1,
[1293](#1293)            msg: msg.into(),
[1294](#1294)        })
[1295](#1295)    }
[1296](#1296)
[1297](#1297)    #[cold]
[1298](#1298)    fn eof_error(&self, expecting: &[Option<char>]) -> Result<char, ParseError> {
[1299](#1299)        self.error(format!("expecting \"{:?}\" but found EOF.", expecting))
[1300](#1300)    }
[1301](#1301)
[1302](#1302)    fn char_or_eof(&self, expecting: &[Option<char>]) -> Result<char, ParseError> {
[1303](#1303)        match self.ch {
[1304](#1304)            Some(ch) => Ok(ch),
[1305](#1305)            None => self.eof_error(expecting),
[1306](#1306)        }
[1307](#1307)    }
[1308](#1308)
[1309](#1309)    fn parse_whitespace_preserve_line_leading(&mut self) {
[1329](#1329)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1330](#1330)            match c {
[1331](#1331)                ' ' | '\t' => {
[1333](#1333)                    self.bump();
[1334](#1334)                    }
[1338](#1338)                '\n' | '\r' => {
[1339](#1339)                    self.bump();
[1341](#1341)                    if matches!(self.ch, Some(' ') | Some('\t')) {
[1343](#1343)                        break;
[1345](#1345)                    }
[1346](#1346)                    }
[1348](#1348)                c if c.is_whitespace() => {
[1349](#1349)                    self.bump();
[1351](#1351)                }
[1352](#1352)                _ => break,
[1353](#1353)            }
[1354](#1354)        }
[1355](#1355)    }
[1356](#1356)
[1357](#1357)    fn parse_whitespace_except_line_break(&mut self) {
[1363](#1363)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1364](#1364)            if (c == '\n' || c == '\r' || !c.is_whitespace()) && c != '\t' {
[1365](#1365)                break;
[1366](#1366)            }
[1367](#1367)            self.bump();
[1368](#1368)        }
[1369](#1369)    }
[1370](#1370)
[1371](#1371)    pub fn parse(&mut self) -> Result<Ini, ParseError> {
[1373](#1373)        let mut result = Ini::new();
[1374](#1374)        let mut curkey: String = "".into();
[1375](#1375)        let mut cursec: Option<String> = None;
[1376](#1376)
[1377](#1377)        while let Some(cur_ch) = self.ch {
[1378](#1378)            match cur_ch {
[1379](#1379)                ';' | '#' => {
[1380](#1380)                    if cfg!(not(feature = "inline-comment")) {
[1381](#1381)                        if self.col > 1 {
[1385](#1385)                            return self.error("doesn't support inline comment");
[1386](#1386)                        }
[1387](#1387)                    }
[1388](#1388)
[1389](#1389)                    self.parse_comment();
[1390](#1390)                }
[1391](#1391)                '[' => match self.parse_section() {
[1392](#1392)                    Ok(mut sec) => {
[1393](#1393)                        trim_in_place(&mut sec);
[1394](#1394)                        cursec = Some(sec);
[1395](#1395)                        match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1396](#1396)                            SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1397](#1397)                                v.insert(Default::default());
[1398](#1398)                            }
[1399](#1399)                            SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1400](#1400)                                o.append(Default::default());
[1401](#1401)                            }
[1402](#1402)                        }
[1403](#1403)                    }
[1404](#1404)                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1405](#1405)                },
[1406](#1406)                '=' | ':' => {
[1407](#1407)                    if (curkey[..]).is_empty() {
[1408](#1408)                        return self.error("missing key");
[1409](#1409)                    }
[1410](#1410)                    match self.parse_val() {
[1411](#1411)                        Ok(mval) => {
[1412](#1412)                            match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1413](#1413)                                SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1414](#1414)                                    let mut prop = Properties::new();
[1416](#1416)                                    prop.insert(curkey, mval);
[1417](#1417)                                    v.insert(prop);
[1418](#1418)                                }
[1419](#1419)                                SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1420](#1420)                                    o.last_mut().append(curkey, mval);
[1422](#1422)                                }
[1423](#1423)                            }
[1424](#1424)                            curkey = "".into();
[1425](#1425)                        }
[1426](#1426)                        Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1427](#1427)                    }
[1428](#1428)                }
[1429](#1429)                ' ' | '\t' => {
[1430](#1430)                    let mut consumed_whitespace = String::new();
[1432](#1432)                    while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1433](#1433)                        if c == ' ' || c == '\t' {
[1434](#1434)                            consumed_whitespace.push(c);
[1435](#1435)                            self.bump();
[1436](#1436)                        } else {
[1437](#1437)                            break;
[1438](#1438)                        }
[1439](#1439)                    }
[1440](#1440)
[1441](#1441)                    match self.ch {
[1443](#1443)                        Some('[') => {
[1444](#1444)                            match self.parse_section() {
[1446](#1446)                                Ok(mut sec) => {
[1447](#1447)                                    trim_in_place(&mut sec);
[1448](#1448)                                    cursec = Some(sec);
[1449](#1449)                                    match result.entry(cursec.clone()) {
[1450](#1450)                                        SectionEntry::Vacant(v) => {
[1451](#1451)                                            v.insert(Default::default());
[1452](#1452)                                        }
[1453](#1453)                                        SectionEntry::Occupied(mut o) => {
[1454](#1454)                                            o.append(Default::default());
[1455](#1455)                                        }
[1456](#1456)                                    }
[1457](#1457)                                }
[1458](#1458)                                Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1459](#1459)                            }
[1460](#1460)                        }
[1461](#1461)                        Some('\n') | Some('\r') => {
[1462](#1462)                            self.bump(); continue;
[1465](#1465)                        }
[1466](#1466)                        _ => {
[1467](#1467)                            match self.parse_str_until(&[Some('='), Some(':')], false) {
[1469](#1469)                                Ok(key_part) => {
[1470](#1470)                                    let mut mkey = if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1471](#1471)                                        consumed_whitespace + &key_part
[1472](#1472)                                    } else {
[1473](#1473)                                        key_part
[1474](#1474)                                    };
[1475](#1475)
[1476](#1476)                                    if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1478](#1478)                                        trim_end_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1479](#1479)                                    } else {
[1480](#1480)                                        trim_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1481](#1481)                                    }
[1482](#1482)                                    curkey = mkey;
[1483](#1483)                                }
[1484](#1484)                                Err(_) => {
[1485](#1485)                                    }
[1488](#1488)                            }
[1489](#1489)                        }
[1490](#1490)                    }
[1491](#1491)                }
[1492](#1492)                '\n' | '\r' => {
[1493](#1493)                    self.bump();
[1495](#1495)                }
[1496](#1496)                _ => match self.parse_key() {
[1497](#1497)                    Ok(mut mkey) => {
[1498](#1498)                        if self.opt.enabled_preserve_key_leading_whitespace {
[1501](#1501)                            trim_end_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1502](#1502)                        } else {
[1503](#1503)                            trim_in_place(&mut mkey);
[1504](#1504)                        }
[1505](#1505)                        curkey = mkey;
[1506](#1506)                    }
[1507](#1507)                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
[1508](#1508)                },
[1509](#1509)            }
[1510](#1510)
[1511](#1511)            self.parse_whitespace_preserve_line_leading();
[1514](#1514)        }
[1515](#1515)
[1516](#1516)        Ok(result)
[1517](#1517)    }
[1518](#1518)
[1519](#1519)    fn parse_comment(&mut self) {
[1520](#1520)        while let Some(c) = self.ch {
[1521](#1521)            self.bump();
[1522](#1522)            if c == '\n' {
[1523](#1523)                break;
[1524](#1524)            }
[1525](#1525)        }
[1526](#1526)    }
[1527](#1527)
[1528](#1528)    fn parse_str_until(&mut self, endpoint: &[Option<char>], check_inline_comment: bool) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1529](#1529)        let mut result: String = String::new();
[1530](#1530)
[1531](#1531)        let mut in_line_continuation = false;
[1532](#1532)
[1533](#1533)        while !endpoint.contains(&self.ch) {
[1534](#1534)            match self.char_or_eof(endpoint)? {
[1535](#1535)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1536](#1536)                ch if check_inline_comment && (ch == ' ' || ch == '\t') => {
[1537](#1537)                    self.bump();
[1538](#1538)
[1539](#1539)                    match self.ch {
[1540](#1540)                        Some('#') | Some(';') => {
[1541](#1541)                            self.parse_comment();
[1543](#1543)                            if in_line_continuation {
[1544](#1544)                                result.push(ch);
[1545](#1545)                                continue;
[1546](#1546)                            } else {
[1547](#1547)                                break;
[1548](#1548)                            }
[1549](#1549)                        }
[1550](#1550)                        Some(_) => {
[1551](#1551)                            result.push(ch);
[1552](#1552)                            continue;
[1553](#1553)                        }
[1554](#1554)                        None => {
[1555](#1555)                            result.push(ch);
[1556](#1556)                        }
[1557](#1557)                    }
[1558](#1558)                }
[1559](#1559)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1560](#1560)                ch if check_inline_comment && in_line_continuation && (ch == '#' || ch == ';') => {
[1561](#1561)                    self.parse_comment();
[1562](#1562)                    continue;
[1563](#1563)                }
[1564](#1564)                '\\' => {
[1565](#1565)                    self.bump();
[1566](#1566)                    let Some(ch) = self.ch else {
[1567](#1567)                        result.push('\\');
[1568](#1568)                        continue;
[1569](#1569)                    };
[1570](#1570)
[1571](#1571)                    if matches!(ch, '\n') {
[1572](#1572)                        in_line_continuation = true;
[1573](#1573)                    } else if self.opt.enabled_escape {
[1574](#1574)                        match ch {
[1575](#1575)                            '0' => result.push('\0'),
[1576](#1576)                            'a' => result.push('\x07'),
[1577](#1577)                            'b' => result.push('\x08'),
[1578](#1578)                            't' => result.push('\t'),
[1579](#1579)                            'r' => result.push('\r'),
[1580](#1580)                            'n' => result.push('\n'),
[1581](#1581)                            '\n' => self.bump(),
[1582](#1582)                            'x' => {
[1583](#1583)                                let mut code: String = String::with_capacity(4);
[1585](#1585)                                for _ in 0..4 {
[1586](#1586)                                    self.bump();
[1587](#1587)                                    let ch = self.char_or_eof(endpoint)?;
[1588](#1588)                                    if ch == '\\' {
[1589](#1589)                                        self.bump();
[1590](#1590)                                        if self.ch != Some('\n') {
[1591](#1591)                                            return self.error(format!(
[1592](#1592)                                                "expecting \"\\\\n\" but \
[1593](#1593)                                             found \"{:?}\".",
[1594](#1594)                                                self.ch
[1595](#1595)                                            ));
[1596](#1596)                                        }
[1597](#1597)                                    }
[1598](#1598)
[1599](#1599)                                    code.push(ch);
[1600](#1600)                                }
[1601](#1601)                                let r = u32::from_str_radix(&code[..], 16);
[1602](#1602)                                match r.ok().and_then(char::from_u32) {
[1603](#1603)                                    Some(ch) => result.push(ch),
[1604](#1604)                                    None => return self.error("unknown character in \\xHH form"),
[1605](#1605)                                }
[1606](#1606)                            }
[1607](#1607)                            c => result.push(c),
[1608](#1608)                        }
[1609](#1609)                    } else {
[1610](#1610)                        result.push('\\');
[1611](#1611)                        result.push(ch);
[1612](#1612)                    }
[1613](#1613)                }
[1614](#1614)                ch => result.push(ch),
[1615](#1615)            }
[1616](#1616)            self.bump();
[1617](#1617)        }
[1618](#1618)
[1619](#1619)        let _ = check_inline_comment;
[1620](#1620)        let _ = in_line_continuation;
[1621](#1621)
[1622](#1622)        Ok(result)
[1623](#1623)    }
[1624](#1624)
[1625](#1625)    fn parse_section(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1626](#1626)        cfg_if! {
[1627](#1627)            if #[cfg(feature = "brackets-in-section-names")] {
[1628](#1628)                self.bump();
[1630](#1630)
[1631](#1631)                let mut s = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\r'), Some('\n')], cfg!(feature = "inline-comment"))?;
[1632](#1632)
[1633](#1633)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1635](#1635)                if matches!(self.ch, Some('#') | Some(';')) {
[1636](#1636)                    self.parse_comment();
[1637](#1637)                }
[1638](#1638)
[1639](#1639)                let tr = s.trim_end_matches([' ', '\t']);
[1640](#1640)                if !tr.ends_with(']') {
[1641](#1641)                    return self.error("section must be ended with ']'");
[1642](#1642)                }
[1643](#1643)
[1644](#1644)                s.truncate(tr.len() - 1);
[1645](#1645)                Ok(s)
[1646](#1646)            } else {
[1647](#1647)                self.bump();
[1649](#1649)                let sec = self.parse_str_until(&[Some(']')], false)?;
[1650](#1650)                if let Some(']') = self.ch {
[1651](#1651)                    self.bump();
[1652](#1652)                }
[1653](#1653)
[1654](#1654)                #[cfg(feature = "inline-comment")]
[1656](#1656)                if matches!(self.ch, Some('#') | Some(';')) {
[1657](#1657)                    self.parse_comment();
[1658](#1658)                }
[1659](#1659)
[1660](#1660)                Ok(sec)
[1661](#1661)            }
[1662](#1662)        }
[1663](#1663)    }
[1664](#1664)
[1665](#1665)    fn parse_key(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1670](#1670)        self.parse_str_until(&[Some('='), Some(':')], false)
[1671](#1671)    }
[1672](#1672)
[1673](#1673)    fn parse_val(&mut self) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1674](#1674)        self.bump();
[1675](#1675)        self.parse_whitespace_except_line_break();
[1677](#1677)
[1678](#1678)        let mut val = String::new();
[1679](#1679)        let mut val_first_part = true;
[1680](#1680)        'parse_value_line_loop: loop {
[1682](#1682)            match self.ch {
[1683](#1683)                None => break,
[1685](#1685)
[1686](#1686)                Some('"') if self.opt.enabled_quote => {
[1688](#1688)                    self.bump();
[1690](#1690)                    let quoted_val = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('"')], false)?;
[1692](#1692)                    val.push_str("ed_val);
[1693](#1693)
[1694](#1694)                    self.bump();
[1696](#1696)
[1697](#1697)                    val_first_part = false;
[1699](#1699)                    continue;
[1700](#1700)                }
[1701](#1701)
[1702](#1702)                Some('\'') if self.opt.enabled_quote => {
[1704](#1704)                    self.bump();
[1706](#1706)                    let quoted_val = self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\'')], false)?;
[1708](#1708)                    val.push_str("ed_val);
[1709](#1709)
[1710](#1710)                    self.bump();
[1712](#1712)
[1713](#1713)                    val_first_part = false;
[1715](#1715)                    continue;
[1716](#1716)                }
[1717](#1717)
[1718](#1718)                _ => {
[1720](#1720)                    let standard_val = self.parse_str_until_eol(cfg!(feature = "inline-comment"))?;
[1722](#1722)
[1723](#1723)                    let trimmed_value = if val_first_part {
[1724](#1724)                        standard_val.trim()
[1726](#1726)                    } else {
[1727](#1727)                        standard_val.trim_end()
[1729](#1729)                    };
[1730](#1730)                    val_first_part = false;
[1731](#1731)
[1732](#1732)                    val.push_str(trimmed_value);
[1733](#1733)
[1734](#1734)                    if self.opt.enabled_indented_mutiline_value {
[1735](#1735)                        self.bump();
[1737](#1737)
[1738](#1738)                        loop {
[1739](#1739)                            match self.ch {
[1740](#1740)                                Some(' ') | Some('\t') => {
[1741](#1741)                                    self.parse_whitespace_except_line_break();
[1744](#1744)                                    val.push('\n');
[1746](#1746)                                    continue 'parse_value_line_loop;
[1748](#1748)                                }
[1749](#1749)
[1750](#1750)                                Some('\r') => {
[1751](#1751)                                    self.bump();
[1753](#1753)                                    if self.ch == Some('\n') {
[1754](#1754)                                        self.bump();
[1755](#1755)                                        val.push('\n');
[1756](#1756)                                    } else {
[1757](#1757)                                        return self.error("\\r is not followed by \\n");
[1759](#1759)                                    }
[1760](#1760)                                }
[1761](#1761)
[1762](#1762)                                Some('\n') => {
[1763](#1763)                                    self.bump();
[1765](#1765)                                    val.push('\n');
[1766](#1766)                                }
[1767](#1767)
[1768](#1768)                                _ => break 'parse_value_line_loop,
[1770](#1770)                            }
[1771](#1771)                        }
[1772](#1772)                    } else {
[1773](#1773)                        break;
[1774](#1774)                    }
[1775](#1775)                }
[1776](#1776)            }
[1777](#1777)        }
[1778](#1778)
[1779](#1779)        if self.opt.enabled_indented_mutiline_value {
[1780](#1780)            trim_line_feeds(&mut val);
[1782](#1782)        }
[1783](#1783)
[1784](#1784)        Ok(val)
[1785](#1785)    }
[1786](#1786)
[1787](#1787)    #[inline]
[1788](#1788)    fn parse_str_until_eol(&mut self, check_inline_comment: bool) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
[1789](#1789)        self.parse_str_until(&[Some('\n'), Some('\r'), None], check_inline_comment)
[1790](#1790)    }
[1791](#1791)}
[1792](#1792)
[1793](#1793)fn trim_in_place(string: &mut String) {
[1794](#1794)    string.truncate(string.trim_end().len());
[1795](#1795)    string.drain(..(string.len() - string.trim_start().len()));
[1796](#1796)}
[1797](#1797)
[1798](#1798)fn trim_end_in_place(string: &mut String) {
[1799](#1799)    string.truncate(string.trim_end().len());
[1800](#1800)}
[1801](#1801)
[1802](#1802)fn trim_line_feeds(string: &mut String) {
[1803](#1803)    const LF: char = '\n';
[1804](#1804)    string.truncate(string.trim_end_matches(LF).len());
[1805](#1805)    string.drain(..(string.len() - string.trim_start_matches(LF).len()));
[1806](#1806)}

[2195](#2195)    fn load_from_str_with_valid_empty_input() {
[2196](#2196)        let input = "key1=\nkey2=val2\n";
[2197](#2197)        let opt = Ini::load_from_str(input);
[2198](#2198)        assert!(opt.is_ok());
[2199](#2199)
[2200](#2200)        let output = opt.unwrap();
[2201](#2201)        assert_eq!(output.len(), 1);
[2202](#2202)        assert!(output.section(None::<String>).is_some());
[2203](#2203)
[2204](#2204)        let sec1 = output.section(None::<String>).unwrap();
[2205](#2205)        assert_eq!(sec1.len(), 2);
[2206](#2206)        let key1: String = "key1".into();
[2207](#2207)        assert!(sec1.contains_key(&key1));
[2208](#2208)        let key2: String = "key2".into();
[2209](#2209)        assert!(sec1.contains_key(&key2));
[2210](#2210)        let val1: String = "".into();
[2211](#2211)        assert_eq!(sec1[&key1], val1);
[2212](#2212)        let val2: String = "val2".into();
[2213](#2213)        assert_eq!(sec1[&key2], val2);
[2214](#2214)    }

[2404](#2404)    fn preserve_order_section() {
[2405](#2405)        let input = r"
[2406](#2406)none2 = n2
[2407](#2407)[SB]
[2408](#2408)p2 = 2
[2409](#2409)[SA]
[2410](#2410)x2 = 2
[2411](#2411)[SC]
[2412](#2412)cd1 = x
[2413](#2413)[xC]
[2414](#2414)xd = x
[2415](#2415)        ";
[2416](#2416)
[2417](#2417)        let data = Ini::load_from_str(input).unwrap();
[2418](#2418)        let keys: Vec<Option<&str>> = data.iter().map(|(k, _)| k).collect();
[2419](#2419)
[2420](#2420)        assert_eq!(keys.len(), 5);
[2421](#2421)        assert_eq!(keys[0], None);
[2422](#2422)        assert_eq!(keys[1], Some("SB"));
[2423](#2423)        assert_eq!(keys[2], Some("SA"));
[2424](#2424)        assert_eq!(keys[3], Some("SC"));
[2425](#2425)        assert_eq!(keys[4], Some("xC"));
[2426](#2426)    }

[2456](#2456)    fn preserve_order_write() {
[2457](#2457)        let input = r"
[2458](#2458)x2 = n2
[2459](#2459)x1 = n2
[2460](#2460)x3 = n2
[2461](#2461)[s]

[2463](#2463)xb = n2
[2464](#2464)a3 = n3
[2465](#2465)";
[2466](#2466)        let data = Ini::load_from_str(input).unwrap();
[2467](#2467)        let mut buf = vec![];
[2468](#2468)        data.write_to(&mut buf).unwrap();
[2469](#2469)        let new_data = Ini::load_from_str(&String::from_utf8(buf).unwrap()).unwrap();
[2470](#2470)
[2471](#2471)        let sec0 = new_data.general_section();
[2472](#2472)        let keys0: Vec<&str> = sec0.iter().map(|(k, _)| k).collect();
[2473](#2473)        assert_eq!(keys0, vec!["x2", "x1", "x3"]);
[2474](#2474)
[2475](#2475)        let sec1 = new_data.section(Some("s")).unwrap();
[2476](#2476)        let keys1: Vec<&str> = sec1.iter().map(|(k, _)| k).collect();
[2477](#2477)        assert_eq!(keys1, vec!["x2", "xb", "a3"]);
[2478](#2478)    }

[2496](#2496)    #[test]
[2497](#2497)    fn write_line_separator() {
[2498](#2498)        use std::str;
[2499](#2499)
[2500](#2500)        let mut ini = Ini::new();
[2501](#2501)        ini.with_section(Some("Section1"))
[2502](#2502)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2503](#2503)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2504](#2504)        ini.with_section(Some("Section2"))
[2505](#2505)            .set("Key1", "Value")
[2506](#2506)            .set("Key2", "Value");
[2507](#2507)
[2508](#2508)        {
[2509](#2509)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2510](#2510)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2511](#2511)                &mut buf,
[2512](#2512)                WriteOption {
[2513](#2513)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::CR,
[2514](#2514)                    ..Default::default()
[2515](#2515)                },
[2516](#2516)            )
[2517](#2517)            .unwrap();
[2518](#2518)
[2519](#2519)            assert_eq!(
[2520](#2520)                "[Section1]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n",
[2521](#2521)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2522](#2522)            );
[2523](#2523)        }
[2524](#2524)
[2525](#2525)        {
[2526](#2526)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2527](#2527)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2528](#2528)                &mut buf,
[2529](#2529)                WriteOption {
[2530](#2530)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::CRLF,
[2531](#2531)                    ..Default::default()
[2532](#2532)                },
[2533](#2533)            )
[2534](#2534)            .unwrap();
[2535](#2535)
[2536](#2536)            assert_eq!(
[2537](#2537)                "[Section1]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n\r\n[Section2]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n",
[2538](#2538)                str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2539](#2539)            );
[2540](#2540)        }
[2541](#2541)
[2542](#2542)        {
[2543](#2543)            let mut buf = Vec::new();
[2544](#2544)            ini.write_to_opt(
[2545](#2545)                &mut buf,
[2546](#2546)                WriteOption {
[2547](#2547)                    line_separator: LineSeparator::SystemDefault,
[2548](#2548)                    ..Default::default()
[2549](#2549)                },
[2550](#2550)            )
[2551](#2551)            .unwrap();
[2552](#2552)
[2553](#2553)            if cfg!(windows) {
[2554](#2554)                assert_eq!(
[2555](#2555)                    "[Section1]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n\r\n[Section2]\r\nKey1=Value\r\nKey2=Value\r\n",
[2556](#2556)                    str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2557](#2557)                );
[2558](#2558)            } else {
[2559](#2559)                assert_eq!(
[2560](#2560)                    "[Section1]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1=Value\nKey2=Value\n",
[2561](#2561)                    str::from_utf8(&buf).unwrap()
[2562](#2562)                );
[2563](#2563)            }
[2564](#2564)        }
[2565](#2565)    }
[2566](#2566)

[2600](#2600)                "Key1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n\n[Section1]\nKey1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n\n[Section2]\nKey1 = Value\nKey2 = Value\n",

[2607](#2607)    fn duplicate_sections() {
[2608](#2608)        let input = r"
[2611](#2611)[Peer]
[2612](#2612)foo = a
[2613](#2613)bar = b
[2614](#2614)
[2615](#2615)[Peer]
[2616](#2616)foo = c
[2617](#2617)bar = d
[2618](#2618)
[2619](#2619)[Peer]
[2620](#2620)foo = e
[2621](#2621)bar = f
[2622](#2622)";
[2623](#2623)
[2624](#2624)        let ini = Ini::load_from_str(input).unwrap();
[2625](#2625)        assert_eq!(3, ini.section_all(Some("Peer")).count());
[2626](#2626)
[2627](#2627)        let mut iter = ini.iter();
[2628](#2628)        let (k0, p0) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2630](#2630)        assert_eq!(None, k0);
[2631](#2631)        assert!(p0.is_empty());
[2632](#2632)        let (k1, p1) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2633](#2633)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k1);
[2634](#2634)        assert_eq!(Some("a"), p1.get("foo"));
[2635](#2635)        assert_eq!(Some("b"), p1.get("bar"));
[2636](#2636)        let (k2, p2) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2637](#2637)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k2);
[2638](#2638)        assert_eq!(Some("c"), p2.get("foo"));
[2639](#2639)        assert_eq!(Some("d"), p2.get("bar"));
[2640](#2640)        let (k3, p3) = iter.next().unwrap();
[2641](#2641)        assert_eq!(Some("Peer"), k3);
[2642](#2642)        assert_eq!(Some("e"), p3.get("foo"));
[2643](#2643)        assert_eq!(Some("f"), p3.get("bar"));
[2644](#2644)
[2645](#2645)        assert_eq!(None, iter.next());
[2646](#2646)    }

[2800](#2800)
[2801](#2801)    #[test]
[2802](#2802)    fn escape_str_basics() {
[2803](#2803)        let test_backslash = r"\backslashes\";
[2804](#2804)        let test_nul = "string with \x00nulls\x00 in it";
[2805](#2805)        let test_controls = "|\x07| bell, |\x08| backspace, |\x7f| delete, |\x1b| escape";
[2806](#2806)        let test_whitespace = "\t \r\n";
[2807](#2807)
[2808](#2808)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_backslash, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_backslash);
[2809](#2809)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_nul, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_nul);
[2810](#2810)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_controls, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_controls);
[2811](#2811)        assert_eq!(escape_str(test_whitespace, EscapePolicy::Nothing), test_whitespace);
[2812](#2812)
[2813](#2813)        for policy in [
[2814](#2814)            EscapePolicy::Basics,
[2815](#2815)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode,
[2816](#2816)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2817](#2817)            EscapePolicy::Reserved,
[2818](#2818)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode,
[2819](#2819)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2820](#2820)            EscapePolicy::Everything,
[2821](#2821)        ] {
[2822](#2822)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_backslash, policy), r"\\backslashes\\");
[2823](#2823)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_nul, policy), r"string with \0nulls\0 in it");
[2824](#2824)            assert_eq!(
[2825](#2825)                escape_str(test_controls, policy),
[2826](#2826)                r"|\a| bell, |\b| backspace, |\x007f| delete, |\x001b| escape"
[2827](#2827)            );
[2828](#2828)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_whitespace, policy), r"\t \r\n");
[2829](#2829)        }
[2830](#2830)    }
[2831](#2831)

[2833](#2833)    fn escape_str_reserved() {

[2836](#2836)        let test_punctuation = "!@$%^&*()-_+/?.>,<[]{}``";
[2838](#2838)
[2839](#2839)        for policy in [
[2841](#2841)            EscapePolicy::Nothing,
[2842](#2842)            EscapePolicy::Basics,

[2844](#2844)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2845](#2845)        ] {

[2847](#2847)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_punctuation, policy), test_punctuation);
[2848](#2848)        }
[2849](#2849)
[2850](#2850)        for policy in [
[2852](#2852)            EscapePolicy::Reserved,
[2853](#2853)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2854](#2854)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode,
[2855](#2855)            EscapePolicy::Everything,
[2856](#2856)        ] {
[2857](#2857)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_reserved, policy), r"\:\=\;\#");

[2863](#2863)    fn escape_str_unicode() {
[2864](#2864)        let test_unicode = r"é£∳字✨";
[2869](#2869)        let test_emoji = r"🐱😉";
[2870](#2870)        let test_cjk = r"𠈌𠕇";
[2871](#2871)        let test_high_points = "\u{10ABCD}\u{10FFFF}";

[2878](#2878)        for policy in [EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicode, EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicode] {
[2881](#2881)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_unicode, policy), r"\x00e9\x00a3\x2233\x5b57\x2728");
[2882](#2882)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_emoji, policy), test_emoji);
[2883](#2883)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_cjk, policy), test_cjk);
[2884](#2884)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_high_points, policy), test_high_points);
[2885](#2885)        }
[2886](#2886)
[2887](#2887)        for policy in [
[2889](#2889)            EscapePolicy::BasicsUnicodeExtended,
[2890](#2890)            EscapePolicy::ReservedUnicodeExtended,
[2891](#2891)        ] {
[2892](#2892)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_unicode, policy), r"\x00e9\x00a3\x2233\x5b57\x2728");
[2893](#2893)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_emoji, policy), r"\x1f431\x1f609");
[2894](#2894)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_cjk, policy), r"\x2020c\x20547");
[2895](#2895)            assert_eq!(escape_str(test_high_points, policy), r"\x10abcd\x10ffff");

[2936](#2936)    fn section_setter_chain() {
[2937](#2937)        let mut ini = Ini::new();
[2940](#2940)        let mut section_setter = ini.with_section(Some("section"));
[2941](#2941)
[2942](#2942)        section_setter.set("a", "1").set("b", "2");
[2944](#2944)        section_setter.set("c", "3");
[2946](#2946)

[2948](#2948)        assert_eq!("2", section_setter.get("b").unwrap());
